title: DevWorks architecture requirement traceability
status: Proposed design coverage, not implemented or tested capability

requirements.statement: Project to repository membership must support multiple repositories. A feature must be able to coordinate work in more than one member repository without pretending there is one shared branch, commit, or PR.
requirements.validationFamily: Domain and relationship invariants
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: All durable records must have stable IDs, scope, actor attribution, timestamps, and revision metadata where editable. Cross-links must survive agent restarts, feature pause, repository reindexing, and conversation changes.
requirements.validationFamily: Domain and relationship invariants
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Feature workflow, card workflow, and agent execution state must be separate. Pausing a coordinator must not move every card to a different workflow column or imply that acceptance has changed.
requirements.validationFamily: Domain and relationship invariants
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The app must own the runtime for its selected capabilities. It must not require CodeGraph, dark-factory, simple-router, MariaDB, RabbitMQ, Docker, or a VM to be installed and administered as supporting servers. Optional container runtimes used by managed projects are separate from this core-app constraint under CONTAINER-01–03.
requirements.validationFamily: Architecture dependency rules
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: UI actions and agent tools must call the same validated Rust application operations. Neither may bypass work-transition rules, revision checks, attribution, or durable history by directly editing storage.
requirements.validationFamily: Architecture dependency rules
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Long-running indexing, provider calls, process output, graph work, and background jobs must not block the UI event loop. Components must publish observable state changes that update open screens incrementally.
requirements.validationFamily: Architecture dependency rules
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: App-managed child processes are allowed for repository commands and optional helpers. A worker process using the same shipped application is a possible isolation mechanism, not a required microservice or account boundary. Final process topology remains open.
requirements.validationFamily: Architecture dependency rules
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The core coordinator and worker harness must be implemented in the Rust application and use its router and tools directly. Running the app must not require a separately installed Claude Code, Codex CLI, or other external agent harness. Optional tool adapters must declare their own dependencies.
requirements.validationFamily: Architecture dependency rules
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The shipped native UI must use egui. Existing HTML artifacts remain design references; selecting egui does not convert the product into a web UI.
requirements.validationFamily: Architecture dependency rules
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The normal desktop configuration must use local embedded storage and persistent in-process scheduling rather than requiring a database daemon or message broker. SQLite must support durable queueing, not just transient in-memory notifications.
requirements.owner: Core storage ports, application transactions and SQLite write owner
requirements.validationFamily: Real-adapter unit-of-work, typed errors, durability and replacement conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A durable queue must support bounded claims, ownership, renewable leases, cancellation, priority, retry policy, terminal failures, and visible status. Restarts must recover pending work without treating every abandoned attempt as safe to replay.
requirements.owner: Application transaction handlers and durable queue
requirements.validationFamily: Atomic claims, history/intent/receipt, fenced ownership and consumer gaps
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Authoritative domain changes, related history and durable queued intent must commit atomically through the application transaction contract. Derived graph, lexical and vector indexes may be prepared asynchronously, with operation identity, idempotent application, generation publication and visible freshness. A saved record must not imply its derived index is already current; database, file and external effects require explicit reconciliation where atomic commit is unavailable.
requirements.owner: Application transaction handlers and durable queue
requirements.validationFamily: Atomic claims, history/intent/receipt, fenced ownership and consumer gaps
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Before retrying an interrupted push, merge, database write or other state-changing tool operation, reconcile what actually happened. Record confirmed completion rather than duplicating it; retry only when the observed state makes that safe. If the coordinator cannot determine an operation outcome, pause the affected operation and dependent work, notify the user and let unrelated work continue. Provider recovery must account for partial output and uncertain request/cost outcomes under existing router policy. Queue deduplication does not prove exactly-once external execution. Reconciliation does not bypass existing manual-resume rules.
requirements.validationFamily: Crash-before/after effect and unknown-outcome hold cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Manual backup and restore under STORE-07 must cover the application database or databases and referenced artifacts at a consistent checkpoint. Define visible scope selection and backup/export controls. Code-derived indexes may be rebuilt; authored knowledge, conversations, instructions, decisions, and execution history must not be treated as disposable indexes.
requirements.owner: StorageMaintenance, artifact lifecycle and restore journal
requirements.validationFamily: Consistent manual images, interrupted restore, stopped restored automation and no implicit backup
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Schema migrations must be versioned and checked before write access. Storage failure, disk exhaustion, incompatible versions, and incomplete recovery must be visible, with preserved data and a diagnosable recovery path.
requirements.validationFamily: Compatibility/checksum gates, rollback, interruption and destructive migration backup guard
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Backups of application databases and artifact files must be initiated manually. Do not run automatic backups.
requirements.owner: StorageMaintenance, artifact lifecycle and restore journal
requirements.validationFamily: Consistent manual images, interrupted restore, stopped restored automation and no implicit backup
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use plain embedded SQLite with sqlite-vec for internal app storage. Persist graph nodes and edges in application-owned tables, with bounded graph traversal/analysis behind the storage contracts and SQLite FTS for lexical search. Do not depend on HelixDB, GraphQLite or a separate graph database for the app. External HelixDB schema reading is excluded under DB-06–07.
requirements.owner: Core storage ports, application transactions and SQLite write owner
requirements.validationFamily: Real-adapter unit-of-work, typed errors, durability and replacement conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: All internal persistence must be accessed through domain-focused repository/query traits and an explicit transaction boundary. Keep SQL, SQLite connections, statements, row mappings, migrations, FTS and sqlite-vec implementation types inside the storage adapter. UI, coordinators, tools, jobs, router and domain/application services must not call SQLite directly or depend on its public types. A replacement data store must preserve the application contracts without rewriting those consumers. External database tools use their separately permissioned target adapters, not raw access to the internal store.
requirements.owner: Core storage ports, application transactions and SQLite write owner
requirements.validationFamily: Real-adapter unit-of-work, typed errors, durability and replacement conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Define shared unit-of-work and read-snapshot contracts. Repositories participating in one logical mutation must share one transaction, preserving atomic domain state, history and durable intent, revision checks and rollback. Query contracts carry scope, pagination, stable identity, provenance and freshness. Do not expose a generic execute-SQL escape hatch or one independently committing repository per table. Keep network calls, inference and long-running computation outside write transactions.
requirements.owner: Core storage ports, application transactions and SQLite write owner
requirements.validationFamily: Real-adapter unit-of-work, typed errors, durability and replacement conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use one SQLite implementation initially and inject it at the application composition root. Require reusable behavioral contract tests against the real adapter, deterministic substitutes for unit tests and no-inference integration tests for transactions, queues, scoped graph/vector queries, publication and recovery. Replacing a store requires another adapter plus validated versioned export/import or migration, preserving identifiers/history/artifact links and the same behavioral suite; replacement is not a hot-swap or an automatic consequence of matching method names.
requirements.owner: Core storage ports, application transactions and SQLite write owner
requirements.validationFamily: Real-adapter unit-of-work, typed errors, durability and replacement conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Graph and search queries must observe a coherent published snapshot with explicit revision/generation identity. Commit writes, deletions and publication must invalidate or version dependent caches; rolled-back changes must not become visible. Test same-connection and cross-connection writes, read snapshots, rollback followed by a new commit, deletion and restart. Scope and overlay filtering must apply before graph expansion or vector materialization; caches must not serve as permission boundaries.
requirements.owner: IndexStore, scoped graph/retrieval views and pins
requirements.validationFamily: Replacement/delete masking, atomic publish, stale builder, scope and cache freshness
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: After restoring an application backup, keep restored schedules and keep-working stopped until the user explicitly reactivates them. Restoring saved enabled states must not start automation or replay old work. Feature and issue work still require explicit selective Continue, and reactivation must reconcile external effects and preserve existing pauses, approvals, budgets and permissions. This is a restore-specific exception to normal scheduled-run resumption on reopening.
requirements.owner: StorageMaintenance, artifact lifecycle and restore journal
requirements.validationFamily: Consistent manual images, interrupted restore, stopped restored automation and no implicit backup
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Tree-sitter must supply baseline structural parsing across project languages. Core code discovery must remain available without optional compiler-backed tooling. Grammar coverage must be explicit: unsupported grammars must yield an honest text-level fallback, not a false claim of semantic support.
requirements.validationFamily: Snapshot/overlay and source-provenance conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Baseline indexing must discover files, structural definitions, source spans, imports, and relationships that can be supported by the grammar and extractor. It must attach repository and revision provenance and identify inferred or unresolved relationships.
requirements.validationFamily: Snapshot/overlay and source-provenance conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Optional semantic support must accept SCIP indexes and enrich the baseline with compiler-backed symbol and reference information. Language packs may also adapt native compiler index formats into the shared code graph, including Swift index stores; SCIP is not the only permitted input. SCIP is an interchange format, not a replacement parser or a guarantee that every language has an available indexer. All adapters must preserve source provenance and report supported and missing capabilities.
requirements.validationFamily: Snapshot/overlay and source-provenance conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide optional compiler-backed semantic language packs for .NET, TypeScript, Swift and Rust. Each pack must declare its supported languages, project types, platforms, toolchain/runtime prerequisites and semantic capabilities. Missing or disabled packs must not prevent application startup or Tree-sitter baseline use. Pack installation does not replace the project toolchain or guarantee that every project can be indexed; unsupported configurations and partial results must be explicit.
requirements.validationFamily: Snapshot/overlay and source-provenance conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Indexing must support incremental updates, file deletion and rename reconciliation, cancellation, progress, failure reporting, and a manual rebuild. Semantic data must record its source revision and must not silently appear current after incompatible source changes.
requirements.validationFamily: Snapshot/overlay and source-provenance conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: CodeGraph-style discovery and context tools must be first-class agent capabilities: structural search, graph traversal, architecture and dependency inspection, source lookup, and contextual retrieval. Agents must not need to operate the old CodeGraph service to use them.
requirements.validationFamily: Snapshot/overlay and source-provenance conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The UI must expose repository index freshness, language coverage, semantic add-in state, source navigation, and the origin of relationships used in agent answers. Cross-repository relationships must preserve each repository’s own revision identity.
requirements.validationFamily: Snapshot/overlay and source-provenance conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Indexing and semantic helpers must have bounded concurrency, memory policies, deadlines, and process-tree cancellation. Deterministic failures must not drive endless retries or leave orphan compiler processes running.
requirements.validationFamily: Snapshot/overlay and source-provenance conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Preserve CodeGraph branch-overlay functionality: query branch/commit changes over the repository baseline without modifying its default-branch index. Automatically include each agent’s uncommitted worktree changes in its graph view, isolated from main and every other worktree. Apply the view consistently to graph search, symbol/source lookup, traversal, dependency/impact inspection and context retrieval. Represent additions, modifications, deletions and renames. Retain repository, branch/commit and worktree provenance, visible freshness and coverage, and inspectable overlay lifecycle and failures.
requirements.validationFamily: Snapshot/overlay and source-provenance conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Identify overlay snapshots by repository, base/head revisions, worktree and local-content version; include staged, unstaged and indexable untracked changes. Select the agent’s own view automatically, with explicit scope for inspecting other views. Incrementally compose changed nodes/edges over unchanged baseline data, hide deleted or renamed-away data, and preserve relation confidence and unresolved links. Publish consistent snapshots atomically; baseline movement or concurrent edits must trigger reconciliation and visible stale/indexing state. Never silently answer a scoped query from main or another worktree, or present baseline-only analysis or stale semantic data as current overlay results.
requirements.validationFamily: Snapshot/overlay and source-provenance conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Expose overlay request/reuse, build/refresh, status, retry and retirement through UI and tools. Show branch/worktree scope and base/head/local-snapshot provenance in graph/source results and indexing logs. Preserve distinct queued, indexing, ready, failed, stale, expired and unavailable states; request reuse must not return incompatible snapshots. Retire derived overlays with owned worktree cleanup while retaining work history and evidence. Define active-overlay retention, expiry and rebuild policy separately from artifact retention. Missing or expired views must produce explicit unavailable/not-indexed results.
requirements.validationFamily: Snapshot/overlay and source-provenance conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Implement optional semantic add-ons as managed executable language packs that can be downloaded and installed without recompiling the main application. The desktop app discovers compatible packs and launches, monitors and stops their helper processes through a versioned extension protocol. No separately administered server, Docker container or VM is required. Harness-owned host and adapter code remains Rust; optional third-party compiler tooling may use its native runtime. Distribute prebuilt helpers for supported OS and CPU targets so installation does not require compiling a Rust crate locally. Cargo features and arbitrary downloaded crates are not the runtime extension mechanism.
requirements.validationFamily: Executable pack protocol and semantic coverage
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide a dedicated Add-ons management screen within Settings for available and installed language packs, including .NET, TypeScript, Swift and Rust. Users must be able to install, update, enable, disable and uninstall packs; inspect versions, language/project/platform support and prerequisites; check dependency and compatibility status; configure pack settings and project enablement; and navigate to indexing progress, errors and logs. Show effective availability separately from configured enablement, including not installed, disabled, missing dependency, incompatible, ready and failed states. Missing or failed packs must leave unrelated work and baseline indexing available.
requirements.validationFamily: Executable pack protocol and semantic coverage
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Define a Rust SDK and a versioned manifest/protocol describing pack identity, publisher/source, version, host API compatibility, platform binaries, languages/project discovery, dependencies, configuration schema and indexing capabilities. Negotiate compatibility before execution. Use a local process transport, such as framed messages over standard input/output, with explicit request IDs, progress/diagnostic events and cancellation. Keep bulk index payloads separate from control messages where needed. Validate downloaded package identity/integrity and install atomically; distribution, publisher trust, update policy and rollback details remain open. New packs can extend declared host capabilities without rebuilding the app; new host extension points or arbitrary native UI behavior may require a host update.
requirements.validationFamily: Executable pack protocol and semantic coverage
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Run semantic packs under app-managed scheduling and existing project/tool permissions. A separate process provides failure containment, not an OS security sandbox. Coordinate helper and compiler process trees with cancellation, resource limits, shutdown and restart recovery under CODE-08 and existing lifecycle rules. Attribute each run to its pack/version, repository, worktree, source snapshot and toolchain. Validate SCIP or native-adapter output before publishing a consistent graph update; reject incompatible or mismatched results and preserve the baseline on failure. Disable/update/uninstall must coordinate active runs and mark affected semantic data unavailable or stale without erasing work history. Define the exact active-run transition and uninstall retention mechanics before implementation.
requirements.validationFamily: Executable pack protocol and semantic coverage
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Opening the app must present a workspace coordinator conversation. The coordinator must be able to discover and inspect every project, feature, card, repository, active agent, relevant conversation, Git action, review, PR, and pending decision within the user’s accessible workspace.
requirements.validationFamily: Current-state delegation and control behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The user must be able to ask for the status of any feature or PR, work across projects, active agents, and everything needing their input. Answers must be connected to the relevant work so the user can open the detailed screen directly.
requirements.validationFamily: Current-state delegation and control behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The workspace coordinator must have tools to create, edit, prioritize, and control project work, and to start, continue, pause, inspect, or redirect the coordinators and workers doing it. Its scope must not be limited to summarization or read-only reporting.
requirements.validationFamily: Current-state delegation and control behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Before answering a consequential status question, it must read current authoritative records and relevant provider state. It must state freshness or uncertainty when unavailable and distinguish a planned step, a tool attempt, an observed result, and a verified outcome.
requirements.validationFamily: Current-state delegation and control behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The coordinator must preserve explicit human directions and explain material consequences of requested changes. It must link actions and status reports to stable work IDs, source evidence, sessions, and artifacts rather than leaving their only record in prose.
requirements.validationFamily: Current-state delegation and control behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Feature execution should be delegated to, or reconciled with, its attached feature coordinator. The workspace coordinator must not silently create a second competing execution owner when the user asks about work already running.
requirements.validationFamily: Current-state delegation and control behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Ambiguous references must be resolved from context where reliable, with clarification only when materially different actions remain possible. Routine reversible work within the user’s policy must not trigger repeated approval prompts.
requirements.validationFamily: Current-state delegation and control behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Workspace conversations must persist independently of feature conversations. New chat must preserve prior sessions and their work links. Starting another workspace chat must not duplicate projects, reset feature context, or launch new agents by itself.
requirements.validationFamily: Current-state delegation and control behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A feature must retain a relationship to every coordinator and worker that has worked on it. Selecting Start must launch an attached feature coordinator to review readiness under AGENT-12; selecting Continue on paused work must resume work with its prior history and current state available.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Start and Continue must be idempotent against already active work. Continuing must preserve logical coordinator identity and session lineage, even if the provider requires a fresh session or a different model. The app must reconcile cards, repositories, instructions, and external effects before new execution.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A feature coordinator must plan and manage cards, delegate scoped assignments, use code intelligence directly, coordinate repository changes, monitor workers, arrange verification and reviews, and keep the feature’s status and history visible.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The execution loop must cover understanding requirements, discovering current code and knowledge, planning dependencies, implementing, validating, reviewing, reconciling findings, and recording acceptance evidence. Existing dark-factory strategies are references to evaluate, not assumed proven solutions.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Worker assignments must identify their originating issue or feature and cards, repository or worktree scope, acceptance criteria, instructions, context, limits, and ownership. Dependencies and resource constraints must be respected before conflicting work is dispatched.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The intended mode is sustained autonomy with almost no routine human interaction. The app must keep working within configured authority and budgets, recover from ordinary failures, and ask for user input when an unresolved conflict or meaningful policy boundary requires it.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A coordinator must not mark work complete merely because an agent says it finished, a command returned success, a PR opened, or a child task stopped. Completion must be checked against the approved requirement and acceptance evidence; unresolved blockers must remain explicit.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Agent coordination must use durable assignments and renewable ownership rather than transcript-only conventions. Retries, stale plans, handovers, dependency changes, and concurrent manual edits must be reconciled with revision checks before work proceeds.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The scheduler must enforce independent per-feature and per-issue subagent limits and coordinate provider capacity, repository writes, compiler/indexing jobs, and other constrained operations. It must expose why work is queued or waiting and avoid dispatching work that cannot run. These operational constraints must not introduce a workspace-wide subagent-count cap.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Settings must provide a configurable maximum number of concurrently active subagents per feature and per standalone issue, defaulting to 10 for each. Each feature and issue has its own independent allowance; there is no workspace-wide or global subagent-count cap. Fewer agents may be used when fewer useful tasks are ready.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Feature coordinators and agents responsible for issues must maximize useful concurrency within the configured limit by running multiple independent, ready tasks at once and refilling capacity as tasks finish. Sequential execution must not be the default when parallel work is available. Dependencies and conflicting writes must be coordinated; a task waiting for user input must not stall independent work.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Before feature implementation starts, its coordinator must assess execution readiness even when the user has already approved the plan. Review the intended outcome and scope, observable acceptance, implementation coverage, dependencies, access and resources, verification and delivery path, and material uncertainties across the whole feature. Every implementation detail need not be settled, but each material uncertainty needs a credible resolution path. On Start, develop incomplete planning from available evidence and seek required plan approval before implementing unapproved scope. Apply AGENT-18–20 to resolve gaps, justify blockers and reuse current assessments. An approved, ready plan must proceed without redundant planning or repeated approval requests.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: After feature-plan approval, the coordinator may adapt task breakdown, delegation, sequencing, scheduling and PR grouping autonomously to complete the feature quickly, efficiently and correctly. Approved requirements and configured concurrency, review and delivery policies still apply. A plan belongs to its feature. Keep the original plan active and approved while a revised plan awaits approval; continue eligible work under it. Approving the revision replaces the active plan; rejection leaves it unchanged. Pending changes cannot authorize new work. Use one active plan and one pending revision, without a user-facing plan-version system. Execution must remain visible and open to user refinement and redirection.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The agent responsible for a standalone issue may delegate scoped work to subagents without creating a feature or manufacturing feature-owned task cards. An assignment may use the issue root and a scoped brief directly; optional linked task records belong to the same project and authorized execution scope. Preserve the parent/child agent relationships, assignments, transcripts, tool actions, changes, reviews and evidence on the issue. Delegated work follows the same router, tool permissions, worktree isolation, visibility and pause/redirect controls as other agent work. Issues use the configurable independent subagent allowance under AGENT-10, defaulting to 10, and maximize useful concurrency under AGENT-11.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A clear, actionable standalone issue may proceed immediately to implementation without separate plan approval. The agent may plan and delegate as needed within the issue’s scope. Ask for input when requirements are unclear or an unresolved decision requires it. Existing tool permissions, user pauses, verification, review and Auto-Merge policies still apply; feature plan-approval requirements remain unchanged.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide an optional per-project keep-working mode that automatically selects and starts the next highest-priority eligible feature or standalone issue through next_work(project). Make its configured state and activity visible and controllable in the project UI. Preserve plan readiness and approval, tool permissions, budgets, resource constraints and existing execution ownership. The mode must not resume explicitly paused work or bypass selective manual Continue after app closure. Run one feature or standalone issue at a time per project in this mode. Its subagents still use the independent per-item allowance under AGENT-10–11, and different projects may work concurrently. After reopening, keep-working requires manual restart. If no eligible work remains, stop until manually enabled again; later queue changes must not restart the mode automatically. Keep-working defaults to off for every new project; enabling it requires an explicit user action.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Every newly started feature, standalone issue or task assignment must begin in a new session with clear context for that work, including when launched by keep-working mode, a scheduled agent or a user action. Assemble the relevant brief, instructions, project knowledge and scoped evidence; do not carry over the prior work item’s conversation as the new session’s transcript. Retain links to the originating action and relevant history without conflating session identities. Continuing an existing item preserves its established history and continuity; it is not a new work item.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The coordinator must resolve what it reasonably can before escalating readiness gaps to the user: inspect current requirements, repository code, project knowledge and conventions; use available evidence and ordinary engineering judgment; and perform bounded investigation within existing authority and budgets. Record the decision and its confidence. A gap blocks affected implementation only when it materially threatens delivery or verification of an approved requirement and cannot reasonably be resolved through those means before that implementation proceeds. Routine reversible technical choices, stylistic preferences and requests for extra detail without a concrete consequence are not blockers. Escalate only remaining material choices or constraints requiring user input, authority or resources, with a specific question and recommended answer. Do not silently narrow approved scope, replace acceptance criteria or invent product intent to avoid escalation.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Record readiness findings against the feature and relevant requirements as resolved decisions, bounded investigations, or matters needing a user decision. Each blocking finding must identify the missing or contradictory requirement/evidence, concrete delivery or verification consequence, affected work, what the coordinator checked or attempted, why autonomous resolution is insufficient, and the specific answer or evidence that closes it. Investigations must have a bounded objective, authority/resource limits, closure evidence and dependent-work gate; they do not authorize unapproved implementation. Keep unrelated eligible work moving. An undefined overall outcome may block the whole feature; a local gap must block only affected work and its dependents. Show the assessment, findings, resolutions and remaining questions through the shared work UI, agent tools and history.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Readiness review has no finding quota; ready with no blockers is valid. Present remaining findings together after reasonable autonomous resolution, then check their closure without repeatedly reopening settled choices. Additional blockers require newly discovered material evidence or changed scope or assumptions. Reuse an assessment while its reviewed plan/scope and relevant evidence remain current; Continue alone does not require another full review. Material changes trigger reassessment of affected scope without invalidating unaffected approved work. Plan approval alone does not clear findings: record resolution or explicit, finding-specific human acceptance of an identified risk. Risk acceptance cannot supply missing prerequisites, make contradictory criteria achievable, waive enforced permissions or required verification, or authorize incomplete work to be reported complete. The feature coordinator remains accountable; a separate reviewer is not universally required.
requirements.validationFamily: Activation, root concurrency and fresh-session tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The user must be able to inspect any active work, its current step, assigned agents, transcripts, tool calls, process output, changes, and results, and interrupt to change direction. The app must not become a closed pipeline whose internal progress is inaccessible.
requirements.validationFamily: Durable redirect stages, admission ordering, scoped cancellation and stale results
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A human instruction must remain linked to the affected feature or assignment and its coordinator transcript. The UI must show that the instruction was sent, acknowledged, and incorporated, rather than silently treating typed text as an executed control action.
requirements.validationFamily: Durable redirect stages, admission ordering, scoped cancellation and stale results
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Pause must stop new dispatch and request safe interruption of active work. Confirmed project archival is an exception under WORK-16: stop immediately without waiting for a safe step. The app must distinguish requested pause, acknowledged pause, and work that has not yet stopped. Cancellation must propagate to owned child processes and streams where supported; incomplete external effects must be reconciled.
requirements.validationFamily: Durable redirect stages, admission ordering, scoped cancellation and stale results
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A redirect must invalidate or supersede incompatible queued work and context at a controlled revision boundary. Late agent results from an older plan must not overwrite newer human edits or be accepted as current completion evidence.
requirements.validationFamily: Durable redirect stages, admission ordering, scoped cancellation and stale results
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: After crash, quit, sleep, connectivity loss, or provider exhaustion, the app must retain conversations, assignments, queue state, checkpoints, outstanding decisions, and known external effects. Resume behavior must be explicit and must not assume an abandoned process completed or did nothing.
requirements.validationFamily: Interruption, hold and stale-result tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Restart must reconcile leases and externally running processes or Git operations before resuming writes. Retries must be bounded and categorized by cause; repeated deterministic failures must stop or escalate with a useful explanation.
requirements.validationFamily: Interruption, hold and stale-result tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A user must be able to inspect why work is paused, blocked, waiting on capacity, rate-limited, failed, or complete. Continue must not erase the condition that prevented progress or bypass an unresolved decision.
requirements.owner: Application eligibility and root execution controls
requirements.validationFamily: Cause-specific blockers, revision-bound Continue and descendant eligibility
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Closing the main application window must pause active agents and background jobs, persist their work and execution state, and exit the application. Work must not continue behind a menu-bar or tray icon after window close. Scheduled jobs do not execute while the app is exited. This explicit shutdown applies to all work; decision escalations remain task-scoped.
requirements.owner: Application lifecycle, supervisor, process host and recovery
requirements.validationFamily: Close/crash/wake recovery classes, boot fencing and uncertain effects
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Shutdown must stop new dispatch, request safe interruption, retain transcripts, checkpoints and queue state, and clean up owned child processes and provider streams with a bounded shutdown policy. In-flight external effects that cannot be confirmed must be marked for reconciliation rather than assumed undone or complete. Feature and issue work require manual resumption on reopening. Enabled maintenance/inference schedules reactivate on reopening, skipping missed occurrences. Interrupted maintenance/inference runs resume automatically; independent pauses, budget holds and approval waits remain. Feature and issue agents still require manual Continue.
requirements.owner: Application lifecycle, supervisor, process host and recovery
requirements.validationFamily: Close/crash/wake recovery classes, boot fencing and uncertain effects
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: After app restart, including a crash, feature and issue work that was active or whose activation was accepted but not launched must remain paused until the user explicitly Continues it. The UI must support selective resumption individually or together; unselected work stays paused. Preserve current instructions, history, unresolved decisions and dependencies, and resume only eligible work. Workspace coordinator chat remains available independently.
requirements.owner: Application lifecycle, supervisor, process host and recovery
requirements.validationFamily: Close/crash/wake recovery classes, boot fencing and uncertain effects
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: When the computer wakes from sleep while the app remains open, previously running feature and issue agents, maintenance jobs and scheduled inference runs must continue automatically. Sleep and wake alone must not introduce a manual-resume requirement. Work already paused or blocked must retain that state; automatic continuation does not clear a user pause or an unresolved decision. Manual feature and issue resumption applies after closing and reopening the app.
requirements.owner: Application lifecycle, supervisor, process host and recovery
requirements.validationFamily: Close/crash/wake recovery classes, boot fencing and uncertain effects
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Paused work requires an explicit, authorized Continue. Start must leave it paused, including calls from the UI, agents and schedules. Agents and schedules may Continue human-paused work only with explicit user authorization; permission to start new work is insufficient. Existing manual-resume rules, permissions and unresolved holds remain effective.
requirements.owner: Application eligibility and root execution controls
requirements.validationFamily: Cause-specific blockers, revision-bound Continue and descendant eligibility
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Continue on a feature or standalone issue resumes its coordinator and all eligible descendant assignments. Child assignments have no manual pause control. Preserve child-specific blockers; continuing the parent must not clear them. Each descendant must pass its own eligibility checks before execution.
requirements.owner: Application eligibility and root execution controls
requirements.validationFamily: Cause-specific blockers, revision-bound Continue and descendant eligibility
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Every application inference request must go through one internal router path, including workspace and feature conversations, worker and review requests, scheduled inference tasks, planning, dreaming, context summarization/compaction, generated titles, semantic enrichment, embeddings, and accepted MCP-initiated inference requests. Agents and application subsystems must not bypass the router to call providers directly.
requirements.validationFamily: One inference boundary, purpose lanes and complete request semantics
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The router must choose suitable agents or models for the job through configurable policies. Its detailed configuration belongs in Settings and may remain hidden during ordinary work. Usage and cost reporting must be a dedicated screen.
requirements.validationFamily: Deterministic provider/routing/budget conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Selection must consider task or role policy, tool and modality support, context size, reasoning effort, availability, provider limits, cost preferences, and session affinity. A user must be able to inspect the selected route and material fallback reason for a request.
requirements.validationFamily: Deterministic provider/routing/budget conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provider adapters must preserve streaming, tool-call identity and ordering, cancellation, errors, supported content types, and resumable conversation semantics. Retries must not duplicate exposed partial responses or repeat externally effective tool calls without reconciliation.
requirements.validationFamily: Framing, terminal state, native call identity and ordered results
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Show provider waiting/failure reasons and the next retry time when known. Honor router-reported cooldowns under ROUTE-15 instead of repeatedly retrying cooling models. Missing authentication and indefinite unavailability need explicit recovery policy. Do not erase the run or route outside configured constraints.
requirements.validationFamily: Classified cooldowns, bounded waits and current eligibility
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Usage must be attributable to project, feature, card or assignment where applicable, coordinator or worker, session, request, provider, model, and role. Router-selected catalog identity and any provider-resolved model identity must remain distinguishable.
requirements.owner: Usage ledger and feature budget admission
requirements.validationFamily: Attribution, cumulative/delta usage, reservation settlement and manual cap resumption
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Reporting must distinguish provider-reported charges, estimated cost, unknown cost, token usage, and subscription capacity. Unknown price must not be represented as zero. A cost preference or routing tier must not be described as an enforced spending cap unless enforcement exists.
requirements.owner: Usage ledger and feature budget admission
requirements.validationFamily: Attribution, cumulative/delta usage, reservation settlement and manual cap resumption
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Each feature supports a spending limit or Off. A reached limit pauses further feature inference; Off tracks spending without a cap. Raising the limit or switching it Off must leave budget-paused work paused until the user manually selects Continue. Continue must still honor other pauses, blockers and current limits. Show attributed spend and effective budget state, preserving incurred usage and visible changes. Exact accounting and in-flight request handling remain open.
requirements.owner: Usage ledger and feature budget admission
requirements.validationFamily: Attribution, cumulative/delta usage, reservation settlement and manual cap resumption
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: When a feature spending limit is configured, begin warning its coordinator at 75% of the budget so it can try to wrap up within the remaining allowance. Keep the warning and remaining-budget information available to the coordinator. Off has no budget-threshold warning. Budget pressure does not waive approved acceptance criteria, required verification or review, or permit incomplete work to be reported as complete.
requirements.owner: Usage ledger and feature budget admission
requirements.validationFamily: Attribution, cumulative/delta usage, reservation settlement and manual cap resumption
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Standalone issues do not support spending limits. Track and display their attributed inference usage and costs, without a per-issue cap, budget-threshold warning or budget-triggered pause. Feature budgets remain feature-scoped. Existing user pauses, approval waits, provider availability and selective manual resume after app closure still apply to issues.
requirements.owner: Usage ledger and feature budget admission
requirements.validationFamily: Attribution, cumulative/delta usage, reservation settlement and manual cap resumption
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Agents must be able to inspect screenshots and other images directly, including chat attachments and stored artifacts. Route image-dependent inference to a model and endpoint that support vision, through the same internal router. Do not silently omit images or claim visual inspection when no capable route is available.
requirements.validationFamily: Deterministic provider/routing/budget conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Pin each session to its initially routed model. Reuse that pin across turns, tool continuations, compaction and app restarts. If rate-limited or unavailable, automatically switch the same session to an available eligible replacement and persist its pin, as in simple-router; retain it after the original recovers. Manual selection persists until changed or failover; Auto restores router selection with pinning. Replacements must meet required capabilities and configured routing constraints. Restoring a pin does not resume feature/issue execution: CONTROL-10 still requires manual Continue. Capability-change and other recovery mechanics remain open; cooldown waits follow ROUTE-15.
requirements.validationFamily: Persisted repin, cursor race and auxiliary lane isolation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: When no eligible model is available and the router reports cooldown expiry times, wait until the earliest eligible model cooldown ends, then automatically recheck availability and reconnect through the router. This temporary wait alone must not require manual Continue. If cooldowns change, honor the updated availability rather than repeatedly retrying early. Pin any replacement under ROUTE-14. Existing user pauses, approval waits, budget holds and app-restart manual-resume rules still apply. Recovery without a reported availability time remains open.
requirements.validationFamily: Earliest applicable reset and no implicit manual hold
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Support Codex, Claude subscription, Anthropic API-key, OpenRouter, and generic OpenAI-compatible connections, using simple-router as the subscription integration reference. OpenAI-compatible connections must accept configurable base URLs and model identities, including Ollama and LM Studio, rather than being limited to named products. Local and remote compatible endpoints must use the same internal router path as the subscription and API-key providers.
requirements.validationFamily: Required provider/endpoint capability matrix
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use simple-router as the reference for provider connection and authentication behavior: Codex subscription device-code sign-in; optional direct Claude subscription browser/authorization-code sign-in at the user's risk, preserving simple-router behavior; a separate Anthropic API-key connection; OpenRouter provider-level API-key management; and optional API keys for configured OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Preserve connection status, token refresh and reauthentication, credential replacement/removal, model discovery/refresh, and connection testing where supported. Expose these controls in native Settings. Claude subscription is unsupported by Anthropic for third-party apps, disabled until explicit user risk acceptance, and distinct from API billing. Never silently exchange subscription and API credentials or billing. The Rust implementation must not require the old router server or external agent CLIs.
requirements.validationFamily: Device/PKCE, refresh, revision races and credential removal
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provider prompt-cache efficiency is a critical harness requirement. Request construction, transcript handling, tool definitions and router behavior must avoid unnecessary harness-induced cache misses. Provider cache availability is not guaranteed; the requirement is to preserve eligible reuse and make its effectiveness observable.
requirements.owner: Context assembler and provider capability profiles
requirements.validationFamily: Native prefix stability, context epochs, cache semantics and observable usage
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use a stable, versioned instruction and tool-definition prefix, with deterministic tool/schema ordering across built-in and MCP tools. Keep changing timestamps, progress, retrieved context and other live state out of the reusable prefix where protocol and instruction authority permit. Persist previously dispatched message/content boundaries and append new turns rather than rebuilding or extending old messages on each request. Meaningful instruction, skill and permission changes still take effect at their required safe step.
requirements.owner: Context assembler and provider capability profiles
requirements.validationFamily: Native prefix stability, context epochs, cache semantics and observable usage
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Preserve native assistant/tool-call/tool-result structure, stable call identities, content-block order and provider-required opaque continuation or reasoning blocks for same-provider continuation. Persist the ordering chosen for concurrent results. Do not flatten tool exchanges into prose, reformat prior results, or discard required continuation data during storage and replay. Cross-provider conversion must be explicit and protocol-correct; do not assume caches or opaque state transfer between providers.
requirements.owner: Context assembler and provider capability profiles
requirements.validationFamily: Native prefix stability, context epochs, cache semantics and observable usage
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provider adapters must declare cache capabilities by actual model, endpoint and access mode, including supported enablement, breakpoint boundaries, keys, minimum lengths, retention and usage fields. Apply supported controls without silently sending incompatible options. OpenAI-compatible syntax or a subscription connection does not imply identical cache support. Preserve eligible session/model/upstream affinity within router policy, while allowing justified quality, capability, availability and policy-driven route changes. Record intentional changes that reduce reuse.
requirements.owner: Context assembler and provider capability profiles
requirements.validationFamily: Native prefix stability, context epochs, cache semantics and observable usage
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Compaction at the confirmed 80% threshold remains mandatory. Preserve stable instructions and reference blocks where possible, record the new compacted context revision, and build subsequent turns append-only from it. Cache optimization must not delay user redirection, retain unauthorized tools, bypass permission enforcement, suppress required fresh context or weaken task correctness. Evaluate total input cost and latency, including cache writes, rather than optimizing hit rate alone.
requirements.owner: Context assembler and provider capability profiles
requirements.validationFamily: Native prefix stability, context epochs, cache semantics and observable usage
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Usage and Costs must show provider-reported cached input, uncached input and cache-write tokens/costs where available, with attribution to requests and work. Distinguish unavailable metrics from zero and estimates from reported values. Provide bounded diagnostics for reusable-prefix changes, tool/instruction revisions, model/upstream changes, compaction and expiry where observable; inferred reasons must be labeled. Avoid duplicate sensitive prompt logging solely for diagnostics. Verify prefix stability and protocol replay across ordinary turns, tool calls, restart, retries, instruction/tool changes and compaction; use live cache metrics where the endpoint exposes them.
requirements.owner: Context assembler and provider capability profiles
requirements.validationFamily: Native prefix stability, context epochs, cache semantics and observable usage
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Regularly check official OpenAI and Anthropic prices and keep the configured pricing catalog current, with visible refresh status and freshness. Provide manual refresh. Preserve the source and price revision used for historical estimates rather than silently repricing old usage when the catalog changes. Exact refresh scheduling and parsing are architecture decisions.
requirements.validationFamily: Weekly freshness, atomic snapshot, parser failure and override preservation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use OpenRouter-reported request costs when available. Treat local-provider usage as free for monetary tracking. For a custom provider, use reported costs or user-configured prices; when neither is available, allow requests and clearly show that price is not tracked, without treating unknown cost as zero or including it in priced totals. Count OpenAI and Anthropic subscription usage toward feature budgets at published API-equivalent estimates, clearly labeled as estimates rather than actual subscription charges. Show the monetary budget coverage and unpriced usage honestly; other budget, pause and permission rules remain effective.
requirements.owner: Usage ledger and feature budget admission
requirements.validationFamily: Reported/estimated/free/untracked cost, coverage and subscription estimates
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Retain native SystemOne decision-model support from simple-router, including models such as Jev: configurable endpoint/upstream identity and credentials, enabled/healthy model discovery, declared question-type and image/video capabilities, structured decision requests/results, bounded errors/cancellation and attributed usage through the shared router. Preserve choice, noul, score and box capability distinctions. Decision models are selected by their own model ID, not offered as chat-generation models or assigned conversational tiers. No old router server is required; native tool access uses the same host authority and accounting as other inference.
requirements.validationFamily: Deterministic provider/routing/budget conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Every chat model selector offers DevWorks Auto under ROUTE-22–24, followed by explicit Tier Max, Tier High, Tier Mid and Tier Low choices, then the named-model group. Allocate eligible configured members in round-robin order: initial Max membership is Fable and Astra; High is Opus and Sol; Mid is Sonnet and Terra; Low is Haiku and Luna. Include eligible custom models assigned to each tier. Membership is editable catalog configuration, not a permanent provider/model inventory. Select a tier directly without translating a named model to a tier. Preserve the resolved session pin across turns and restart under ROUTE-14–15; round robin applies when allocating or replacing a pin. Named-model selection requests that model directly. Offer Open Router Auto and Auto Beta as distinct explicit OpenRouter upstream routes, not synonyms for DevWorks Auto or tier selection; they bypass local tier classification. Context, capabilities, effort, enabled state, health and current policy still determine eligibility; do not silently cross to another tier or invent support when a pool is empty.
requirements.validationFamily: Deterministic provider/routing/budget conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide reasoning effort as a separate selector alongside the route/model selector in every chat composer, including the shared Home/sidebar session. Persist the selected effort independently of tier or model. Advertise and send only the effort values supported by the configured model, endpoint and access mode; preserve requested and effective effort in route/usage diagnostics. A nondefault explicit effort is an eligibility constraint and cannot silently disappear on failover. Provider Default is a separate choice. Model labels must not encode effort, and changing effort must not itself change tier membership or derive another tier from a model name.
requirements.validationFamily: Deterministic provider/routing/budget conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Support a configurable pool of multiple SystemOne decision models, separate from conversational tiers. Each new automatically selected logical decision request takes the next eligible pool member in durable round-robin order and never creates or reuses a session pin. Filter by declared question/media/input capabilities, enabled state, usable connection, authorization, availability and current policy. Preserve direct model-ID invocation for callers deliberately selecting a decision model. Concurrent allocation and restart retain the cursor and request identity; receipt replay reuses a known decision rather than dispatching another inference.
requirements.validationFamily: Deterministic provider/routing/budget conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Offer DevWorks Auto as a distinct route selection. Immediately before a new session's first generation request, classify the required tier from its initial prompt, role, task/assignment and authorized project context using a versioned, inspectable rubric. The only valid tier answers are Low, Mid, High and Max. Prefer an eligible SystemOne decision model under ROUTE-21. Explicit named-model and tier selections bypass classification. Explicit upstream auto routes, including OpenRouter Auto and Auto Beta, bypass DevWorks tier classification and retain their configured upstream identity. Preserve existing saved selections and defaults unless explicitly changed; new worker sessions receive their own initial assignment.
requirements.validationFamily: Deterministic provider/routing/budget conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: If no SystemOne model is usable for the initial tier decision, use the next eligible Low-tier generation model as an auxiliary classifier through the shared router. This classifier request targets Low directly, has no conversational pin, and cannot recursively invoke tier selection. Treat malformed/non-tier answers, missing capabilities, authentication, exhausted credits, cooldowns, capacity and transport failures honestly. Attempts are bounded per model; other model successes cannot reset a failing model's retry limit. Try eligible decision candidates before falling back, and eligible Low candidates within a bounded pass; if neither path yields a valid decision, wait or refuse with a concrete reason rather than inventing a tier. Attribute classifier and generation attempts separately under existing authority, cost and feature-budget controls.
requirements.validationFamily: Deterministic provider/routing/budget conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Persist a successful DevWorks Auto tier decision and its policy/input provenance, then allocate and pin an eligible generation model within that tier. Classify once per new session, not once per turn. Ordinary messages, tool continuations, compaction, restart, policy edits and later complexity changes must not reclassify or automatically change the tier. Persist an already chosen tier even if generation must wait for availability. Reuse the eligible generation pin; a necessary availability replacement stays within the chosen tier, is explained and persists. If that tier cannot meet a new required capability, surface the limitation without silently changing tier. Manual named-model or tier changes remain explicit exceptions; restarting or resuming work still obeys existing holds. Restoring a previously established automatic assignment never reclassifies it; a manually started session without one needs a new session to obtain an automatic tier assignment. Explicitly auxiliary titles, embeddings and other purpose-routed inference do not establish or invalidate the conversational automatic assignment.
requirements.validationFamily: Deterministic provider/routing/budget conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide stable -latest aliases for OpenAI Astra (Max), Sol (High), Terra (Mid), Luna (Low), and Anthropic Fable (Max), Opus (High), Sonnet (Mid), Haiku (Low). Refresh complete provider model lists hourly while the app is open, recheck overdue lists on reopening, and retain manual refresh. Resolve each family alias to the highest available numeric version in its configured provider/connection scope, promoting newly listed higher versions automatically. If the highest version disappears, use the highest version still listed; if none remains, the alias is unavailable. Compare parsed version components, not lexical order, response order or discovery time. Preserve connection/billing boundaries and configured allow/exclude constraints.
requirements.owner: Shared model discovery and alias/pin resolution
requirements.validationFamily: Hourly complete catalogs, numeric promotion/fallback, reversible availability, selection and concrete pin preservation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: For all providers and models, including custom and SystemOne decision models, reconcile availability from successful complete model-list refreshes. Keep missing model records, user enablement/configuration and historical references; mark them unavailable for new selection and routing, and restore availability when they return without re-enabling user-disabled models. Failed, malformed or partial refreshes must not become authoritative shorter catalogs. Availability is scoped to the serving connection and remains distinct from user enablement, authentication, cooldowns and request-specific capability eligibility.
requirements.owner: Shared model discovery and alias/pin resolution
requirements.validationFamily: Hourly complete catalogs, numeric promotion/fallback, reversible availability, selection and concrete pin preservation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Every model-selection input, particularly Workspace/Home chat and its shared sidebar, offers the eight family -latest aliases alongside available explicit versions. New/replacement tier assignments round-robin across the configured latest aliases for those eight families, retaining configured custom tier members outside them. Preserve editable tier membership, independent effort and direct named-version/upstream-auto choices. Allocate once per chat and persist its resolved concrete version pin across turns, tool continuations, compaction and restart; an alias promotion alone neither invalidates an eligible pin nor reclassifies its Auto tier. Unavailable pins use normal eligible same-tier replacement. Alias intent, concrete catalog identity and provider-resolved identity remain distinguishable, and known request replay does not re-resolve an alias or consume another round-robin turn.
requirements.owner: Shared model discovery and alias/pin resolution
requirements.validationFamily: Hourly complete catalogs, numeric promotion/fallback, reversible availability, selection and concrete pin preservation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Project work must have full manual visibility and control. The feature list must support creation, editing, search, filters, prioritization, and access to in-progress, paused, ready, and completed work. Project membership and feature repository scope must be editable.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Each feature must have a visible Kanban board for planning cards. Humans and agents must be able to create, edit, reprioritize, assign and move tasks, and add or remove task-blocking dependencies through shared operations. This includes standalone issues and tasks in different features of the same project. Priority selects among eligible tasks; an unresolved prerequisite keeps a dependent task blocked regardless of priority. Accessible controls must accompany drag and drop.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: All core project, feature, and card management operations exposed to the user must also be controllable through first-class agent tools, using the same domain rules. An agent action must appear in the same board and history as a manual action.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A feature must hold requirements, acceptance criteria, description, priority, workflow state, repository scope, coordinator relationship, and related artifacts. A planning card must hold its own type, description, priority, workflow state, assignment, dependency links, acceptance criteria, and repository context.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Dependency checks must prevent invalid cycles and identify blocked or stale prerequisites. A manually completed card must remain distinguishable from completion supported by verified acceptance evidence where those differ.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Concurrent edits must use revision checks. A stale manual form or late agent update must be refused or explicitly reconciled while preserving the user’s draft. Silent last-write-wins behavior is unacceptable for instructions, planning state, and conflict resolutions.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Ordinary archiving or removing work from a current view must preserve its history and links. Permanent project deletion is a separate explicit action under WORK-15. Repository removal from a project must not delete files, branches, transcripts, or evidence, and must explain active references before changing membership.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The user must always be able to refine a feature plan, both before execution and while agents are working, through direct management controls or coordinator conversation. Refinements must remain linked to the feature and its plan/history. The feature coordinator must review and incorporate changes into the current plan rather than treating the initial plan as permanently fixed.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result
