requirements.statement: Provide next_work(project, feature = null). Project is required. With feature omitted or null, select the highest-priority eligible feature or standalone issue from one project queue. Feature selection requires approval for implementation; skip incomplete or unapproved plans. Explicit Start may still initiate feature planning. Feature tasks are not separate project-queue candidates; with feature supplied, select the highest-priority eligible task within that feature and project. Scheduled agents may allocate/start work under these rules. Clear actionable standalone issues retain their existing no-separate-plan-approval policy.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Allocate the highest-priority eligible work atomically with durable caller/session ownership; concurrent callers must not receive the same assignment. Use runtime request identities for idempotent retries, and expose selection/assignment, work kind/ID, version and no-eligible-work reasons. Validate that a feature belongs to the project. Respect dependencies, active ownership, explicit pauses, budget holds and approval waits. Define stable priority tie-breaking and lease/recovery semantics. Selection/claim and execution start are distinct; use the existing Start/coordinator path without duplicate coordinators or silently resuming user-paused features. Transfer ownership visibly to the feature coordinator or assigned worker and retain schedule/run provenance, context and Git/history links.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Every task belongs to a project and may optionally belong to a feature; standalone tasks are issues with the same durable identity. Humans and agents can create, manage and directly start tasks without requiring a feature, retaining their sessions, transcripts, Git/review, artifacts and activity history. Humans and agents may link and unlink issues. Linking makes resolution part of feature delivery and authorizes that addition without revised-plan approval. An existing agent notifies the feature coordinator and continues; otherwise the coordinator launches or resumes work when eligible. Existing pauses and blockers remain. Unlinking pauses work until manually resumed. Future spending uses the feature budget; earlier costs remain attributed where incurred. Keep existing branches/workspaces; the coordinator owns integration. Direct feature transfers continue under the new coordinator/budget while retaining holds.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide project issue browsing/filtering, New issue with optional feature membership, and shared UI/chat/tool set/clear operations guarded by work revisions and project membership. Capture title, description/reproduction, expected/actual behavior where known, priority, status, acceptance criteria, repositories and source issue. Preserve one identity and its agent/session, transcript, Git/review, artifacts and history across association changes. Reconcile queues, supervisor responsibility, budget attribution and delivery routing without duplicate execution. Feature-linked work uses coordinator delivery; standalone work uses existing issue policies. Editable task details expose priority, blockers, Start/Pause/Continue, agents and history. Unlink uses a durable pause; relinking cannot clear it. Issue restart, concurrency and delegation retain CONTROL-10, AGENT-10–11 and AGENT-14.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Support custom Kanban columns and status names per project. Users must be able to manage their project workflow instead of being restricted to fixed global columns. Feature boards and project issues must use the applicable project statuses, with the same workflow available to agents through first-class tools.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Give project statuses stable identities and explicit workflow semantics for allocation, readiness, review and completion; agents and next_work must not infer behavior solely from editable display names. Provide column creation, renaming and ordering with equivalent tool operations. Removing an occupied status requires an explicit destination for affected work, preserving history. Keep workflow status separate from execution pause/wait state; moving a card must not bypass plan approval, checks, reviews or merge policy. Refine the exact status mapping and transition rules before implementation.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared UI/tool work transition and ownership tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Removing a project from active management must archive its records and history by default. Preserve its work records, linked agent sessions, transcripts, decisions, Git/review history and evidence under the existing retention rules. Permanent deletion must be a separate explicit action, never a side effect of archiving or ordinary project removal. Provide the same project-management behavior through the UI and permitted first-class tools under WORK-03.
requirements.validationFamily: Close/wake/archive/manual resume and no-resource-deletion boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: If any agents are actively working on a project when archival is requested, warn the user and ask whether they are sure they want to archive it before proceeding. Declining leaves the project and its work unchanged. On confirmation, stop all project work immediately: block new dispatch and interrupt active coordinators, subagents, inference/tool operations, owned processes and background work without waiting for a safe step, task completion or a cooperative checkpoint. Archived projects must not start new work through keep-working, project schedules or other dispatch paths. Retain recorded history and interrupted-work state; unrelated projects continue. This applies to archival initiated through the UI or agent tools. Restoring an archived project must leave its work, keep-working mode and project schedules stopped until the user explicitly reactivates them. Restoration alone must not resume execution.
requirements.validationFamily: Close/wake/archive/manual resume and no-resource-deletion boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Permanent project deletion must remove only its harness data and artifacts. Leave local repositories, including their files, worktrees and branches, and all GitHub resources untouched. Deletion must not trigger repository cleanup or remote GitHub mutations. Apply the same boundary to the UI and permitted agent tools; ordinary archival remains nondestructive under WORK-15. Preserve shared artifacts while another project still references them. Shared-data ownership and deletion mechanics remain to be specified.
requirements.validationFamily: Close/wake/archive/manual resume and no-resource-deletion boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: From a feature, task, or related project work, the user must be able to browse the full linked history of coordinators and workers, transcripts, tool actions, Git actions, reviews, merge requests or PRs, decisions, and outcomes.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Lineage, source identity and retained-link tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: History must be a durable queryable relationship graph and event record, not a concatenated log alone. Events must identify actor, work scope, operation, timestamp, relevant repository and revision, and linked evidence. Corrections and reversals must preserve prior records.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Lineage, source identity and retained-link tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Source control overview must preserve repository boundaries inside a project and feature. Branches, worktrees, changed files, diffs, commits, PRs, checks, reviews, and merge state must be attributed to their actual repository.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: All agent coding and integration work must use Git worktrees. Each concurrent coding task must have its own isolated worktree for each repository it changes; tasks must not share a writable working tree or edit the primary checkout. The feature coordinator integrates task changes using a worktree. Worktree ownership must remain linked to the task, agent, history and feature where applicable. Preserve existing user changes without requiring separate OS accounts or a VM.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Source-control views must support inspection of repository and branch state, changes/diffs, commits, worktrees, PRs, checks and review findings, with links to the producing agent session. Built-in manual staging, committing, branch management and merging are not required; the user uses an external Git client or GitHub for those operations. This does not remove the harness’s configured autonomous Git and delivery capabilities.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Automated commits, pushes, PR creation or updates, reviews, conflict resolution, and merges must follow configured authority and branch policies. A multi-repository feature must track its integration dependencies and each repository’s result without claiming an atomic merge across repositories.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Reviews and verification evidence must identify the source revision they assess. New changes must invalidate or refresh relevant conclusions. Successful tool completion must not be reported as passing checks, review approval, or merge success without observed evidence.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: When a feature completes, automatically remove all harness-created worktrees and local branches associated with that feature across every involved repository, including task and integration worktrees/branches. Retain transcripts, commit identities, PR/review links, and the historical ownership records after the local Git resources are removed.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Before cleanup, verify resource ownership and integration evidence and stop any remaining writers. Cleanup must not discard uncommitted work or unintegrated commits, or remove unrelated user resources. Record each result; expose failures and a retry path instead of silently reporting successful cleanup. Paused features retain the worktrees needed for continuation.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Features must always use a feature branch in each affected repository. Task PRs target that feature branch. The feature coordinator chooses whether related tasks share a PR or have separate PRs; one PR per task is not required. Open the final feature PR to main only once the feature implementation is complete, never as an early task-delivery path. The final feature PRs remain linked to the same feature and its task/group PR history.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Distinguish implementation completion, final PR delivery, and cleanup in execution state and the UI. Implementation completion permits the final feature PR to main; review/fix/check and Auto-Merge policies still govern its merge. Keep needed worktrees and branches while final delivery is pending. Run feature-completion cleanup after final integration is verified across the affected repositories, and show cleanup failures explicitly. This sequencing preserves the required branch while its final PR is open.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Every task must document its associated current worktrees, branches and PRs so the user can easily find where its work lives. Show the repository, worktree path, branch name and PR link on the task, including each relevant repository for cross-repository work. Grouped-task PRs must be linked from every covered task. Preserve historical associations after cleanup and distinguish removed or closed resources from current ones.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Standalone issues use an isolated task branch and worktree and open PRs directly to main. They do not require a feature branch. Preserve configured review/fix/check and Auto-Merge policy and show branch/worktree/PR links on the issue. Tasks belonging to features retain the existing feature-branch delivery flow.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: After verified merge of an issue to main, automatically clean up its harness-owned worktrees and local branches. Retain transcripts, artifacts, GitHub links and complete work history. Preserve unintegrated work and show cleanup failure/retry state under GIT-07.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Agents may automatically force-push their own task branches, including after a rebase. Force-pushing feature branches requires explicit user approval; branches outside an agent-owned task branch must not receive automatic force-push authority. Never force-push to main. This prohibition applies regardless of Auto-Merge settings, package/tool configuration or an approval for another operation, and must cover equivalent forced updates to the main ref. Existing repository access controls and branch protections remain in effect; approval does not authorize bypassing them. Record permitted force-pushes, approvals, denials and outcomes in the linked task/feature and agent history.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Before a force-push, resolve the actual repository, remote and destination ref, check task-branch ownership and effective branch protection, and validate any required approval against that concrete operation. Use an explicit expected remote revision with force-with-lease or an equivalent guarded update so concurrent remote changes cause refusal and reconciliation rather than overwrite. Unknown ownership must not qualify for automatic authority. Enforce the main prohibition for harness-dispatched Git operations, including forced refspecs and equivalent invocation forms. Define preflight, shell/tool enforcement and approval-binding mechanics, preserving the absolute main prohibition under GIT-13.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: For a feature spanning multiple repositories, all final feature PRs must pass their required checks and reviews before any final PR is merged. Once every final PR is ready, merge them in dependency order. Apply each repository’s effective Auto-Merge, review and approval policies; readiness does not grant authority to merge when that authority is disabled or awaiting approval. Track each repository’s delivery result and the feature’s overall delivery history.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Resolve routine merge conflicts autonomously and continue delivery without notifying the user or requesting routine conflict-resolution approval. Concurrent agents working in the same repository are expected to cause conflicts; the coordinator must reconcile their changes while preserving the approved feature requirements. Conflict resolution does not waive required checks, reviews, repository merge authority or the prohibition on force-pushing main. If a merge fails in an unusual way that the coordinator cannot resolve, pause the affected delivery and dependent work and notify the user with the failure, attempts and evidence. Independent work continues; ordinary recoverable conflicts are recorded in history without a user notification.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A feature is complete once all of its final feature PRs are verified as merged into main across the affected repositories. Track releases and deployments separately, retaining links to the feature, repositories, revisions and delivery history. A pending, approval-waiting or failed release or deployment must not keep the merged feature open. Release and deployment actions retain their separate configured authority under DELIVERY-09. Feature completion triggers the required cleanup of harness-owned worktrees and local branches under GIT-06–09; retain the feature’s history and artifacts and expose cleanup outcomes separately.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Real temporary Git and controlled GitHub delivery cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Every project must have a local artifact store for screenshots, files, reports and other work outputs. Agents must be able to save, discover and read artifacts through first-class tools and share stable references with other agents and humans. Humans must be able to add and inspect files through the UI. Artifacts must retain explicit links to their originating project and, where applicable, feature and task, with navigation from that work to the artifact and back. Later reuse must preserve those origin links.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Atomic file/reference publication and retained-share tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Give each artifact stable identity and metadata for name, media type, size, tags, creation time, producing agent/session, feature/task and relevant repository revision. Preserve source relationships and versions instead of silently overwriting referenced evidence. Show attachments in conversations, task/feature history and a searchable project Artifacts view, with image/text previews and file open/export controls.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Atomic file/reference publication and retained-share tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Store artifact contents as local files managed outside disposable worktrees, SQLite metadata and graph provenance links. Publish complete files atomically and preserve references across restart, agent handoff and Git cleanup. Feature completion must not delete its artifacts when branches and worktrees are removed. No separate object-storage server or cloud account is required.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Atomic file/reference publication and retained-share tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Artifact access must honor project scope and effective tool policy, including read-only reviewers. Supply bounded previews or file references to agents rather than inserting every file into model context. Define storage location, quotas and deletion behavior in Settings; retain artifacts until explicitly deleted under ART-05 and show disk/write failures. Include contents and metadata in backup/restore and avoid silently deleting referenced evidence.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Atomic file/reference publication and retained-share tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Keep project artifacts until explicitly deleted. Automatic expiration or cleanup must be disabled by default; artifact age, feature completion, worktree cleanup and storage pressure must not silently remove retained files. Storage limits must produce visible status rather than implicit deletion.
requirements.sourceSection: 12 Source control and complete work history
requirements.validationFamily: Atomic file/reference publication and retained-share tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Chat is the primary app-wide interface. Place existing navigation on the left, the active workspace coordinator conversation in the center, and a right sidebar with Current first and Chat History second. Current is selected initially. Overview remains specific to the selected project. Do not replace the sidebar with a conversation dropdown.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The center conversation must support a persistent composer, readable messages and tool or result summaries, and links to the work being discussed. The initial state must invite a conversation with workspace-wide scope. Keep the integrated Workspace coordinator header; omit the redundant conversation-name row and Across your projects status strip because Current supplies that information. Align the plus attachment button, model/tier and effort controls with Send along the bottom of the workspace input. Below its border, show All projects followed by the pinned model on the left and the send keyboard hint on the right; omit redundant Workspace coordinator text. Preserve usable wrapping at narrower sizes. Every composer retains attachments under UI-08 and routing/effort under UI-10.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The right sidebar must provide Current and Chat History tabs without disrupting the conversation. Current shows app-wide Needs you, Working and Recently completed, with project labels and direct links to affected work. Chat History shows prior workspace conversations, the active selection, search and useful date grouping. Keep New Chat in the persistent center header beside Coordinator instructions, available with either tab selected. Tab changes and navigation preserve the active session, per-chat draft, attachments and relevant scroll positions; session selection restores the correct transcript. Feature coordinator conversations remain attached to their features.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The user must be able to leave chat to inspect a detailed screen and return without losing the conversation, its session selection, or its connection to ongoing work.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Coordinator role instructions, workspace scope, and relevant context must be inspectable. Detailed routing configuration must remain in Settings, while request attribution and cost may be inspected when useful.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Place the app-wide Approvals destination directly below Chat in the left navigation, with an all-project inbox and project filtering. Activity belongs inside the project-specific Overview as a section with filters and full history, rather than a separate left-navigation destination. Keep Intelligence navigation collapsible without losing access to its screens.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use the approved Workspace coordinator / Overview visual language across every page and secondary view: warm neutral surfaces, bordered content groups, consistent type, spacing and quieter secondary actions. Integrate each page header into its primary content pane, with one continuous outer border and a divider into the body; do not use a detached full-width header card. Secondary panes start alongside the header. Place inner sidebars on the right for Approvals, Knowledge entries/documents, Dreaming run history and Databases. Complete the same grouping and header treatment for Repositories, Agents, Artifacts, Knowledge, Dreaming and all Database states/views. Overview and Features summary values and labels sit inline with matching baseline, size and spacing directly beneath the integrated header. Left-align the version and update message at the bottom of the left sidebar. Preserve existing capabilities and navigation/selection/filter/scroll behavior.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Every long-running operation must expose current state, progress where meaningful, cancellation or pause where supported, and recoverable errors. Empty, loading, offline, partial-data, failed, and stale-data states must be designed rather than represented as fabricated success or zero values.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Keyboard navigation, readable focus states, screen-reader labels, text scaling, accessible status changes, and large histories must be supported. Resize behavior must preserve the conversation and essential controls. Theme customization and exact native pane sizing remain open; the shared visual direction follows UI-15.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Every chat input must accept images and files through a selection dialog, drag-and-drop and paste. Apply this to workspace, feature, issue and every other interactive agent chat composer. Attachments must accompany the correct message and remain accessible from its conversation history; image inspection follows ROUTE-13. Use a plus-only attachment button with an accessible name and tooltip explaining that it attaches images or files.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Show pending attachments with filenames and image previews where supported; allow removal before sending and preserve them with per-chat drafts. Store durable copies and stable attachment references, retaining conversation and applicable project/feature/task provenance through the artifact system. Workspace attachments without a project retain their conversation scope until associated with work. Define file formats, size limits, clipboard handling and extraction; show unsupported or failed processing rather than pretending unread content was analyzed. Preserve original attachments through context compaction and provider changes.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Every chat input must include a selector populated with configured router tiers and available named models under ROUTE-19, plus a separate effort selector under ROUTE-20. Tier Max, High, Mid and Low precede the named model group; Open Router Auto selects the OpenRouter automatic route directly. Selection and effort persist for the chat and are shared between Home and its sidebar. Tier allocation pins its resolved model until changed or replaced by eligible failover under ROUTE-14–15. All requests still pass through the router and respect permissions and required capabilities.
requirements.validationFamily: Native view/composer/control identity tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide Help as a first-class menu/navigation item near Settings. It must open a searchable documentation workspace and remain readily accessible from the main interface. Every screen and Settings section must include a contextual Help link that opens its relevant local documentation topic.
requirements.owner: Local Help service and capability registry
requirements.validationFamily: Offline/topic/version/coverage checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Document every aspect of the working system, including every UI screen, action and setting; project/repository/work/agent workflows; planning, approvals and delivery; routing and context; knowledge and skills; indexing and graph/schema exploration; jobs, containers and integrations; artifacts, storage and lifecycle; and diagnostics, recovery, permissions and limitations. Explain actual behavior, defaults, configuration scope and practical use. Documentation is a core product capability and must be maintained with the functionality it describes.
requirements.owner: Local Help service and capability registry
requirements.validationFamily: Offline/topic/version/coverage checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Document all supported extensibility points and how to create plugins/add-ins, including harness packages and semantic language packs. Provide developer guidance for SDKs, manifests, protocols, tools/commands, workflows/events, context/instruction extensions, native UI contributions and router/provider adapters where supported. Cover prerequisites, development/build/test, packaging, installation/configuration, permissions and approvals, compatibility/versioning, updates, troubleshooting and rollback, with usable examples. Distinguish supported contracts from unimplemented or unsupported capabilities.
requirements.owner: Local Help service and capability registry
requirements.validationFamily: Offline/topic/version/coverage checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Make system and extension documentation accessible to agents through first-class search/read tools so coordinators, workers and read-only reviewers can learn and use the system they operate. Humans and agents must access the same maintained documentation. Documentation retrieval follows configured tool permissions and must not grant authority or override user directions. Agent access must cover UI behavior as well as tools and extensibility, not just tool schema descriptions.
requirements.owner: Local Help service and capability registry
requirements.validationFamily: Offline/topic/version/coverage checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Help must live entirely locally and offline, bundled and versioned alongside the app and installed add-ons. Match app documentation to the installed app version and add-on documentation to the installed add-on version. Human browsing/search and agent documentation search/read tools must operate on this local content without requiring a network connection, hosted documentation service or remote search fallback.
requirements.owner: Local Help service and capability registry
requirements.validationFamily: Offline/topic/version/coverage checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use stable topic identifiers and contextual links from errors; screen and Settings-section Help links are required under HELP-01. Let agents retrieve bounded passages with topic/version references instead of injecting the entire manual into each session. Review documentation coverage and examples alongside capability changes, and expose missing, stale or unavailable documentation. Exact local authoring format, search/indexing, packaging/update mechanics and documentation checks remain to specify; offline-only content and version matching are confirmed under HELP-05.
requirements.owner: Local Help service and capability registry
requirements.validationFamily: Offline/topic/version/coverage checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The user must have one Knowledge workspace consolidating memory, knowledge and lessons, differentiated by tags. It must support inspection, tag search and filtering, manual creation and editing, lifecycle changes, and source evidence. Agents must use the same connected knowledge system through tools.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Tagged identity, source revision and scope tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Memory must represent entities and atomic claims with predicates, values, scope, evidence, author or agent provenance, confidence, timestamps, and revision history. Conflicting observations must remain inspectable until resolved; confidence must not be presented as proof.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Tagged identity, source revision and scope tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Knowledge must support goals, decisions, constraints, facts, gotchas, attempts, architecture notes, and lessons, with active, superseded, or retracted lifecycle states as appropriate. Verification must record the evidence and source revision used, and later source changes must be able to mark entries stale. Each decision records who made it. A decision the user made or approved, including one approved in chat and recorded by an agent, names the user as its origin; only a decision an agent made on its own is marked autonomous. Autonomous decisions stay visible for reading and never ask the user to acknowledge them; the review queue under REVIEW-01 holds only conflicts an agent cannot resolve.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Tagged identity, source revision and scope tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Lessons and rules must be visible with their origin, applicability, recurrence, challenges, and relationship to the work where they were learned or used. Agents must be able to retrieve and manage them through tools.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Tagged identity, source revision and scope tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The lesson lifecycle must distinguish candidate evidence, proposed rules, effective rules, and rejected proposals. Human instructions, review-derived lessons, and repeated corrections must retain their distinct provenance; recurrence alone must not be treated as proof of effectiveness. A rule’s origin decides how it takes effect. A rule from the user’s own instruction or review, given directly or relayed by an agent with the user’s words attached, takes effect immediately without approval; it is the user’s own edit under EVAL-05 and is monitored under EVAL-07. A lesson inferred by an agent, subagent or automated reviewer stays candidate evidence until it recurs across a configured number of distinct source events, then takes effect automatically without approval and is monitored under EVAL-07 like any other change that takes effect without approval under EVAL-05. No rule asks the user for approval; the user may promote a candidate early, or challenge or retire any rule, at any time. Taking effect is not proof that a rule works. Eval evidence under EVAL-08 may show whether a lesson rule is effective.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Tagged identity, source revision and scope tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Rule delivery must be inspectable: the app must record which relevant rules and revisions were supplied to a session. It must expose whether a lesson has been addressed in code, instructions, a skill, documentation, or a test, and surface unmatched or unlearned evidence where useful.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Tagged identity, source revision and scope tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: General lessons must be available across projects automatically without manual sharing or promotion for each project. Project-specific knowledge and conventions must remain scoped to their project. Shared lessons must retain their origin and applicability; automatic availability does not make every lesson relevant to every task. Project-scoped content must remain scoped in agent retrieval and context assembly, including when dreaming consolidates it.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Tagged identity, source revision and scope tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Consolidate memory, knowledge and lessons into one Knowledge system and workspace, differentiated by tags rather than independent catalogs. Preserve identity, evidence, relationships, revisions and applicable learning metadata without duplicating the same item across categories. Scope remains a separate property: a lesson tag alone must not share project-specific content. Human and agent tools must support the same tagging and scoped retrieval operations.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Tagged identity, source revision and scope tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Context assembly must combine the work brief, current plan, instructions, relevant code and graph results, scoped knowledge, applicable lessons, prior evidence, and handover state within a deliberate token budget. It must preserve provenance instead of indiscriminately replaying all repository content and chat history.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Instruction, token-accounting and compaction fixtures
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A session must record its instruction revisions, retrieved context sources, important omissions or truncation, and routing metadata sufficiently to explain what information the agent acted on. Context updates and summaries must preserve unresolved constraints and decisions.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Instruction, token-accounting and compaction fixtures
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Resolve enforced permissions and explicit user directions before repository guidance. Applicable repository instructions override default role instructions. Resolve repository conflicts by nearest directory first, only within its subtree; at one directory AGENTS.md overrides CLAUDE.md, whose nonconflicting instructions still apply. Preserve nonconflicting ancestor rules. Discover only authorized instruction roots, retain exact source digests/applicability in each effective context and reconcile material unresolved conflicts visibly. Same-level ambiguity cannot grant authority or silently affect another repository.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Instruction, token-accounting and compaction fixtures
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: When an agent reaches 80% of the active model’s maximum context, the harness must automatically compact its working context and continue without user intervention. Preserve the complete original transcript and the same logical agent identity and work relationships. Compaction must not replace or truncate the stored transcript; record the compaction and resulting continuation in the agent’s session history. Any compaction inference must use the router.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Instruction, token-accounting and compaction fixtures
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Measure context against the actual routed model/endpoint limit, including instructions, tool schemas, messages and tool results with appropriate modality accounting. Reserve response/tool headroom and check request size before dispatch, including after model changes. Compaction must preserve current requirements, plan state, user directions, unresolved decisions and relevant evidence/artifact references. Unknown limits, oversized single inputs and failed compaction need visible bounded recovery rather than silent truncation or loss of work.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Instruction, token-accounting and compaction fixtures
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Automatically load applicable repository and subdirectory AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md instructions. Instructions closest to the target files override conflicting ancestor instructions within that subtree. At the same directory level AGENTS.md wins conflicts; CLAUDE.md adds nonconflicting guidance. Repository instructions override default role instructions. User directions and enforced permissions remain above all file instructions. Preserve path applicability across multiple directories/repositories; files cannot grant tool authority.
requirements.sourceSection: 15 Context memory knowledge lessons and rules
requirements.validationFamily: Instruction, token-accounting and compaction fixtures
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Dreaming must consolidate and maintain memory, knowledge, and lessons with visible runs and outcomes. The user must be able to inspect what was considered, what changed, what was proposed, and what remains unresolved.
requirements.validationFamily: Journaled consolidation, conflicts and guarded revert
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Dreaming must have inspectable base and project instructions with revision history, manual and scheduled triggers, budgets, cancellation, and bounded execution. Every run must record the instruction revisions, source scope, usage, actual outcome, and errors or unfinished work.
requirements.validationFamily: Journaled consolidation, conflicts and guarded revert
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Dreaming must verify against current evidence, preserve provenance and human corrections, and separate direct permitted changes from proposals requiring review. Dispatch success must not be reported as successful consolidation. Partial and budget-exhausted runs must remain distinguishable from completed runs.
requirements.validationFamily: Journaled consolidation, conflicts and guarded revert
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Direct changes must have an action journal with before and after revisions and a guarded revert path. A revert must not overwrite subsequent human or agent edits; conflicts must be reported and proposals must remain separately identifiable.
requirements.validationFamily: Journaled consolidation, conflicts and guarded revert
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Dreaming must automatically apply consolidations when there is no conflict, without requesting approval for each change. Preserve the visibility and project-scoping requirements. Conflicts an automated agent cannot resolve must enter the review queue and notify the user; independent non-conflicting consolidation can continue.
requirements.validationFamily: Journaled consolidation, conflicts and guarded revert
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The app must provide an approval or review queue for conflicts an automated agent cannot resolve. Items must show the competing records or proposed change, evidence, origin, affected project and work, and the decision required from the user.
requirements.validationFamily: Revision-bound attributed decisions and task-scoped holds
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The queue must distinguish a human-escalated decision from a proposal that an authorized agent can review. Agents must not impersonate a human resolution. Resolution must retain actor, rationale, revisions, and resulting changes, with expected-version checks against the records being resolved.
requirements.validationFamily: Revision-bound attributed decisions and task-scoped holds
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: An escalation must pause only the task needing user input and work dependent on that task or merge. Agents must continue unblocked tasks in the feature. The entire feature should wait only when that merge blocks the remaining feature work. Resolving one item must not clear unrelated conflicts; existing instructions remain effective while a proposal is pending.
requirements.validationFamily: Revision-bound attributed decisions and task-scoped holds
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: In-app notifications must surface required input and other meaningful work events, with direct links to their project, feature, session, review, or report. Notifications must be available from the main chat and detailed workspaces.
requirements.validationFamily: Inbox/deduplication/deep-link/OS-permission checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The global inbox must support read and unread state, category filtering, and duplicate suppression. Reading or dismissing a notification must not resolve its linked review item. Resolution and acknowledgment are separate operations.
requirements.validationFamily: Inbox/deduplication/deep-link/OS-permission checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Notification policy should cover decisions, failures, blocked work, significant completions, review changes, budget or authentication problems, and dreaming reports. Feature and issue completion presentation follows confirmed NOTIFY-05. Severity, quiet preferences, aggregation and OS alerts for other categories remain open; required-input OS alerts follow NOTIFY-04.
requirements.validationFamily: Inbox/deduplication/deep-link/OS-permission checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: When the app is not focused, items needing user input must also trigger native operating-system notifications where supported and permitted. Respect OS authorization and notification suppression. Keep the in-app notification and approval item available if OS alerts are denied, unavailable or suppressed. Displaying, reading or dismissing an OS notification must not resolve the decision. Native integration and per-platform behavior require validation.
requirements.validationFamily: Inbox/deduplication/deep-link/OS-permission checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Verified feature and issue completions must produce highly visible in-app cards floating at the top center below the global toolbar on Chat and every other page. Cards must not reserve layout space, shift content, steal focus or obstruct essential controls. Stack new messages like playing cards, newest first, with access to expand and inspect every message. Keep each card until the user explicitly dismisses it, including across navigation and restart; opening or reading linked work must not dismiss it. Dismissal removes only that card from the stack and retains the notification in history. Provide direct links to completed work, avoid duplicate completion events, and preserve keyboard access, accessible status announcements and reduced-motion behavior. Dismissal or acknowledgment must not resolve approvals or resume work.
requirements.validationFamily: Inbox/deduplication/deep-link/OS-permission checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Minimum OS targets are macOS 26.2 and Windows 10. Linux is also required, with supported distributions and versions to be determined during architecture validation from what the chosen components can support. Do not claim every Linux distribution is supported. Core installation and launch must not require preinstalled .NET, Node or Python. The same primary Rust codebase must provide the selected behavior; CPU architectures, packaging formats and the validated compatibility matrix remain to specify.
requirements.validationFamily: Clean machine target/dependency audit
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The application must work without an app server or separately administered storage infrastructure. Local browsing, planning edits, and history inspection must remain useful without provider connectivity. Provider-dependent actions must show their actual waiting or failure state.
requirements.validationFamily: Clean machine target/dependency audit
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Dependency claims must distinguish the app runtime from optional semantic helpers, Git, repository build toolchains, and optional local inference. The app must detect missing tools and state exactly which operation needs them; optional components must not become accidental startup requirements.
requirements.validationFamily: Clean machine target/dependency audit
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The app must feel fast, modern, and lightweight. Startup, idle memory and CPU, installed size, active indexing, graph queries, transcript scrolling, and multiple concurrent agents must be measured separately rather than summarized by a single unverified footprint claim.
requirements.owner: Native UI, engine and adapter owners
requirements.validationFamily: Representative resource and latency measurements
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: UI lists and transcripts must scale through incremental updates and bounded rendering. Indexing, vector caches, process output retention, provider concurrency, and background schedules must have visible resource controls. Numeric targets and benchmark datasets remain open.
requirements.owner: Native UI, engine and adapter owners
requirements.validationFamily: Representative resource and latency measurements
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use one normal desktop user context. Store secrets through appropriate OS facilities, redact them from ordinary logs, and show what project content is sent to external providers. A separate local web login and OS user switching must not be part of ordinary use.
requirements.validationFamily: Effect classification, scope and destructive-path adversarial cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Autonomous filesystem, shell, network, Git, and integration access must be governed by explicit project scope and user policy, with attribution and interruptibility. A Git worktree provides write isolation, not a security sandbox. Any stronger optional isolation must not recreate mandatory VM infrastructure.
requirements.validationFamily: Effect classification, scope and destructive-path adversarial cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Make agent access and trust restrictions configurable, supporting broad/full-access use as well as users who prefer tighter restrictions. Full access is the initial default for new projects; tighter access remains selectable. Show effective permissions and access mode in Settings. Existing role restrictions, including always-read-only code reviewers, explicit approvals and the prohibition on force-pushing main remain effective; full access does not waive them. Configuration scope and OS-enforced isolation options require architecture validation without mandatory VM infrastructure.
requirements.validationFamily: Effect classification, scope and destructive-path adversarial cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide basic safety checks on tool calls to prevent accidental deletion of entire drives or repositories. Keep these checks active even for full-access agents. Check destructive operations before dispatch, expose blocked operations and their rationale, and preserve attribution in the relevant work history. These are additional guards, not replacements for configured tool permissions. Drive/filesystem roots remain blocked. Deliberate deletion of a registered primary repository requires a dedicated user-confirmed action; agents cannot bypass this with operation approval or full access.
requirements.validationFamily: Effect classification, scope and destructive-path adversarial cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Centralize safety preflight for built-in and brokered shell/process, MCP and package tool calls. Resolve actual deletion targets, including path roots, parent traversal, wildcards and links/reparse points; protect filesystem/volume roots and registered repository roots. Avoid relying only on literal command-name or string matching. Distinguish bounded cleanup of owned task worktrees from deletion of a primary repository. Define enforcement for opaque tools and native executable add-ons honestly: harness policy checks alone do not provide OS confinement against arbitrary code running with the user’s permissions. Validate any stronger claimed restriction at the process/OS boundary. Rule coverage, bypass resistance and platform-specific enforcement remain architecture validation work.
requirements.validationFamily: Effect classification, scope and destructive-path adversarial cases
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The app must provide local diagnostics for storage, queue health, orphan processes, indexing, provider failures, and recovery. Data export, backup/restore, schema migration, and update behavior must preserve authored records and explain failures.
requirements.validationFamily: Data preservation, observability and no-server audit
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The app must not require a central product account or remote control plane for normal operation. Repository hosting and provider integrations may use their own credentials. Provider connections follow ROUTE-09–10; Git-host authentication methods still need selection and documentation.
requirements.validationFamily: Data preservation, observability and no-server audit
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide first-class agent tools for testing websites through browser control and for testing native desktop applications through computer control. UI tests must exercise the application under development and expose their activity and results in the harness. Browser control does not change the native egui UI decision.
requirements.validationFamily: Browser/native control conformance and OK/Wait behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use browser DOM/accessibility targets and native accessibility controls where available, with screenshots and pointer/keyboard input when needed. Native automation needs platform adapters and explicit permission/capability status on macOS, Windows and Linux. Unsupported controls or missing permissions must produce visible limitations rather than false test success.
requirements.validationFamily: Browser/native control conformance and OK/Wait behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Link UI test sessions, actions, screenshots, assertions, failures and relevant browser/process logs to the feature, task, responsible agent and tested repository revision. The user must be able to inspect, interrupt and redirect testing. Record observed outcomes; completing an input action alone does not prove a workflow passed.
requirements.validationFamily: Browser/native control conformance and OK/Wait behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Isolate concurrent browser sessions and test data. Coordinate access to shared desktop focus, mouse and keyboard through the resource reservation system under RES-01–03 so agents cannot interfere with each other. This resource constraint must not become a global subagent-count cap. If the user is active, desktop takeover requires OK or Wait under UIQA-05; idle detection and approval lifetime remain open. Mutating UI tests must run under an authorized testing/implementation role, preserving always-read-only reviewers.
requirements.validationFamily: Browser/native control conformance and OK/Wait behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Before taking control of a desktop that is not idle, ask the user and offer OK or Wait. OK authorizes the pending takeover; Wait defers it and must not be treated as approval. Do not inject input or steal focus while awaiting the answer or after Wait. Show the request and waiting state in the app. Independent feature work must continue. Idle detection and retry mechanics remain to be specified.
requirements.validationFamily: Browser/native control conformance and OK/Wait behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide a resource reservation system modeled on CodeGraph resources and holds, exposed through first-class tools and visible in the UI. Support named resources with capacity, acquire, renew and release operations, resource/holder/waiter inspection, purpose, priority, expiry and ownership linked to the feature, task and agent session. Reservations coordinate finite resources such as desktop input, test environments, ports, databases and constrained hardware; they are distinct from per-feature and per-issue subagent limits.
requirements.validationFamily: Capacity, fencing and physical-owner reconciliation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use a canonical resource identity across projects for physically shared resources, including one machine desktop. Scope project-private resources separately. Enforce ownership and capacity at harness-controlled operation dispatch for resources such as desktop input; CodeGraph advisory holds alone are insufficient to prevent concurrent input. Queue unavailable resources by priority and FIFO within a priority; unrelated tasks continue.
requirements.validationFamily: Capacity, fencing and physical-owner reconciliation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Persist reservation state and use atomic allocation, idempotent retries and explicit renewal. Track grant, release, expiry, cancellation, queue position and unreachable ownership. An expired lease does not prove its process stopped: stop or reconcile old writers and reject stale owners before transferring a physical resource. Show recovery and reservation history in the UI, including pause, shutdown and sleep/wake reconciliation.
requirements.validationFamily: Capacity, fencing and physical-owner reconciliation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide an application update function using GitHub Releases from the repository where this application will be hosted. While the app is open, automatically poll that repository every hour for a newer release. The product repository is SceneWorks/DevWorks at https://github.com/SceneWorks/DevWorks; use its GitHub Releases for update discovery. Update checking must not require a separate application server or a background harness process after exit.
requirements.validationFamily: Signature, asset, restart and schema compatibility fixtures
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Always display the currently installed application version in the lower-left sidebar. When a newer release is available to download, indicate its availability in that same lower-left area and provide access to the download/update action. Continue showing the installed version while an update is available or downloaded; only an applied update changes that displayed current version.
requirements.validationFamily: Signature, asset, restart and schema compatibility fixtures
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Distinguish update checking, available, downloading, staged, applying and failed states. Resolve the correct OS/CPU release asset, validate version and artifact integrity, show progress and retry/cancel where applicable, and preserve the working installed version on failed download or preparation. Update the bundled local Help with the corresponding app version. Preserve work/state and existing shutdown/manual-resume rules during installation/restart; self-improvement activation still requires explicit approval under SELF-03. Automatic background download and approval before installation/restart are confirmed under UPDATE-04. The architecture adopts stable releases by default with explicit prerelease opt-in, due launch/hourly checks, signed staging and approved installation/restart. Native offline/rate-limit, signature and platform installation/rollback qualification remains required.
requirements.validationFamily: Signature, asset, restart and schema compatibility fixtures
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Automatically download newly available application updates in the background. Require explicit user approval before installing the update and restarting the app. Release discovery or a completed download must not count as that approval. While approval is pending or declined, retain the running installed version and allow existing authorized work to continue. Apply approved updates with the existing work-preservation, shutdown and selective-resume rules; include the matching local Help version.
requirements.validationFamily: Signature, asset, restart and schema compatibility fixtures
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Settings must expand into a substantial categorized screen covering the required topics. It must remain accessible from the existing navigation while keeping chat as the opening interface.
requirements.validationFamily: Scope/inheritance/revision/conflict and safe-boundary tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Settings must provide discoverable categories and search, show configuration scope and effective values, validate edits, preserve unsaved changes, and distinguish configured values from connection health or runtime availability. Exact subnavigation and placement remain design decisions.
requirements.validationFamily: Scope/inheritance/revision/conflict and safe-boundary tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Settings must let the user inspect, edit and save instructions for every agent role, including workspace coordinator, feature coordinator, worker, code reviewer and dreaming. Edited instructions must remain subject to harness-enforced policies, including mandatory read-only reviewers; prompt edits cannot grant tools or override those policies. Active agents adopt edits at their next safe step under SET-04; repository instructions take precedence over default roles under user directions and enforced permissions.
requirements.validationFamily: Scope/inheritance/revision/conflict and safe-boundary tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Running agents must adopt user-saved or approved edits to their role instructions at their next safe step, without requiring a new session or manual restart. Unapproved agent proposals must not take effect. Retain the instructions used for completed work and preserve effective tool restrictions, user directions and unresolved blockers.
requirements.validationFamily: Scope/inheritance/revision/conflict and safe-boundary tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Agents may draft changes to their role instructions, but explicit user approval is required before applying or activating those changes. Preserve version history and provide rollback. Approved changes reach active agents at their next safe step under SET-04; pending or rejected proposals leave the current instructions effective. Approval does not override user directions or configured tool permissions.
requirements.validationFamily: Scope/inheritance/revision/conflict and safe-boundary tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Stage agent-authored skill and role-instruction proposals separately from active files, using the approval queue and notifications. Show the affected scope, file changes, rationale, agent/work provenance and validation. Bind approval to the reviewed revision; changed proposals or concurrent user edits require reconciliation. Record approval/rejection and application outcomes. Apply only approved changes, retain prior versions, and keep unrelated authorized work running while approval is pending.
requirements.validationFamily: Scope/inheritance/revision/conflict and safe-boundary tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide an app-wide preferred base directory for local repositories in Settings, with an optional override per project. Projects without an override inherit the app-wide default. Users must be able to choose their preferred repository location rather than rely on a fixed application path.
requirements.validationFamily: Scope/inheritance/revision/conflict and safe-boundary tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide a directory chooser and editable path, persist the repository base directory and report invalid or unavailable locations. Use it as the default destination for new repository clones while retaining support for repositories located elsewhere. Changing the setting must not move existing repositories or alter their recorded paths. Keep this setting distinct from harness artifact storage and worktree placement. Show the effective directory and whether it is inherited or overridden. Default path and clone-destination naming remain open.
requirements.validationFamily: Scope/inheritance/revision/conflict and safe-boundary tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide an app-wide preferred container-system setting with optional per-project overrides, supporting Docker and Podman for projects that require containers. Projects without an override inherit the app-wide backend; clearing an override restores inheritance. Harness tools must honor the selected backend for container operations rather than require Docker for all projects. Container runtimes are optional project dependencies, not prerequisites for starting or using the harness itself.
requirements.validationFamily: Selected-runtime capabilities and owned stop behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Offer Apple’s first-party container tooling as an additional backend on supported Macs where feasible. Detect supported OS/CPU and installed tooling and clearly show unavailable or unsupported states. Do not describe it as a universally preinstalled macOS capability. Rust host code may integrate with the optional external tool; no Swift development toolchain is required merely by choosing this backend. Validate the supported operation set before claiming parity with Docker or Podman.
requirements.validationFamily: Selected-runtime capabilities and owned stop behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use backend adapters for image build/pull, container create/start/stop, command execution, inspection and logs, reporting supported operations explicitly. Show selected versus effective backend, executable/connection, version, health and errors in Settings. Record project/work/agent attribution, coordinate shared ports and other resources, and enforce existing tool permissions and read-only reviewer restrictions. Require normal system-install approval for installing runtimes. Do not silently substitute another backend or assume OCI-image compatibility guarantees Compose, networking, volume or Docker API compatibility. Closing the app stops agent-work containers under CONTAINER-04. Initial backend default, multi-service support, ownership/recovery mechanics and container lifecycle across pause, archive and deletion remain open.
requirements.validationFamily: Selected-runtime capabilities and owned stop behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: When the app closes, stop containers launched for agent work. Leave pre-existing and manually managed containers running. Preserve attribution so shutdown targets the agent-work containers rather than stopping the selected engine or all of its containers. Stopping is not permission to delete containers, images, volumes or stored data. Exact ownership detection, stop failure/recovery and restart behavior remain to specify.
requirements.validationFamily: Selected-runtime capabilities and owned stop behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Settings must provide a keep-awake option, off by default, on macOS, Windows and Linux. While enabled and the app is open, prevent idle system sleep even without active work, but allow the display to turn off. Closing the app ends its keep-awake request.
requirements.validationFamily: Idle-sleep inhibition/display/exit policy checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use the operating system power-management facility to request prevention of idle system sleep. Show the configured value and whether the request is effective or unavailable; disabling the option releases the request. Do not imply that it prevents explicit sleep, lid-close behavior, shutdown, or every OS power policy. The setting defaults to off and allows display sleep under POWER-01.
requirements.validationFamily: Idle-sleep inhibition/display/exit policy checks
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Support both MCP directions: connect to external MCP servers alongside first-class built-in tools, and expose a DevWorks MCP server for other clients and harnesses. Users manage external server configurations and select the capabilities available to DevWorks agents. The earlier client-only decision is superseded.
requirements.validationFamily: Outgoing capability integration plus incoming transport, grant, scope, publication and recovery conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The supported transport and capability matrix must be explicit. Configure app-launched local processes and remote server connections where supported, with executable/arguments or endpoint, environment, working directory, authentication references, connection testing, start/stop or reconnect, capability discovery, and failure diagnostics.
requirements.validationFamily: Outgoing capability integration plus incoming transport, grant, scope, publication and recovery conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result
