requirements.statement: MCP tools must retain server identity and schemas, avoid name collisions, follow the same access policy and attribution rules as built-in tools, and link invocation inputs, results, failures, timeouts, and external effects to the responsible agent session and work.
requirements.validationFamily: Outgoing capability integration plus incoming transport, grant, scope, publication and recovery conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: External servers may need optional runtimes such as Node or Python. The app must show those dependencies and failures explicitly without making them prerequisites for launching or using core functionality. Missing or unhealthy servers must not stall unrelated work.
requirements.validationFamily: Outgoing capability integration plus incoming transport, grant, scope, publication and recovery conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Tool discovery, server capability changes, resources and prompts where supported, and any server-initiated inference requests need an explicit compatibility and authority policy. Inference initiated through this integration must still follow the application router. This requirement governs outgoing client integration; incoming clients use the DevWorks server boundary under MCP-07–11.
requirements.validationFamily: Outgoing capability integration plus incoming transport, grant, scope, publication and recovery conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: When an MCP server is added, enable its read-only tools by default. Users must be able to choose which tools are available through individual toggles and an easy Select all control. Automatic enablement applies to read-only tools; other tools become available through user selection. Show the effective selection in Settings.
requirements.validationFamily: Outgoing capability integration plus incoming transport, grant, scope, publication and recovery conformance
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Other MCP-compatible clients and harnesses must be able to use DevWorks indexed code, planned work and Knowledge. Preserve code search, architecture/dependency/source retrieval, plans/features/issues/tasks and their histories, and Knowledge claims/evidence/conventions/document retrieval with the same scope, freshness and provenance as first-class application tools.
requirements.validationFamily: Independent-client context parity, authenticated scope, explicit command grants and recovery
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide native stdio and Streamable HTTP access through a server adapter to the shared application gateway. Stdio uses a small installed bridge to the running desktop app; HTTP is opt-in and loopback-bound. Closing the app makes the server unavailable and must not leave a daemon or a second store writer. Publish version-qualified setup instructions and an explicit protocol/capability compatibility matrix.
requirements.validationFamily: Independent-client context parity, authenticated scope, explicit command grants and recovery
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Incoming clients require individually authorized, revocable identities and explicit project/repository/worktree scopes. Default grants allow selected reads only. Human configuration controls connection approval, credential provisioning, tool/resource visibility and any write grants. Check current authority before invocation and publication; protocol metadata, client labels, tool annotations and resource URIs cannot grant authority. Credentials and private application/package transports are never exposed.
requirements.validationFamily: Independent-client context parity, authenticated scope, explicit command grants and recovery
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Allow explicitly selected work and Knowledge mutations through existing typed commands, revisions, approvals, attribution, idempotency receipts and recovery rules. An external harness cannot impersonate a human, self-grant permissions, bypass reviewer restrictions or clear human-only execution holds. Index refresh or inference is an explicit separately granted command, never a hidden effect of context retrieval. Keep external inference and provider credentials owned by the external harness unless it explicitly invokes an authorized DevWorks operation.
requirements.validationFamily: Independent-client context parity, authenticated scope, explicit command grants and recovery
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Expose discoverable tools and scoped resources, with optional context prompts, bounded pagination/results and precise unsupported or unavailable outcomes. Preserve view/source identity, citations, coverage gaps and work revisions; support cancellation and durable status/receipt recovery after disconnection without duplicate effects. Qualify at least two independent clients across both transports, including revoked scopes, isolated overlays, denied writes and restart behavior before advertising compatibility.
requirements.validationFamily: Independent-client context parity, authenticated scope, explicit command grants and recovery
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The app must provide GitHub configuration and integration as a supported product capability, with visible account/host configuration, repository associations, authorization status, and access to linked PRs, checks, and code reviews.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: GitHub credentials, token scopes and failures must be inspectable without exposing secrets. Git transport credentials and GitHub API authorization must be distinguished. Use the single GitHub.com account and organization support under GH-03. Use direct API polling under GH-10. Authentication method and additional Git hosts remain open; multiple-account and Enterprise support are not required by the agreed scope.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Support one GitHub.com account, including personal repositories and repositories owned by organizations the account can access. Organization-owned repositories must support discovery, project association and the same authorized PR, check, review and delivery workflows as personal repositories. Preserve repository owner identity and respect actual account and repository permissions; organization support must not require signing in as another user.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Always display references to GitHub resources as clickable links to the corresponding resource. Apply this across coordinator/agent messages, task and feature details, source-control views, activity/history, reviews, notifications and other app surfaces. This includes repositories, branches, commits, issues, PRs, reviews and checks/workflow runs when referenced. Use identifiable labels with repository/owner context where needed; a bare resource number, name or hash must not substitute for the link.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: For linked GitHub issues, automatically reflect remote updates in local tracking. Keep intermediate execution details local. Once work is completed and verified, automatically post a resolution summary and close the GitHub issue. Verify and use clarification about the same bug; genuinely new scope or feature requests require a user decision. Remote closure does not stop a verified bug already being fixed or approved/planned feature work. Close the local copy of an unstarted unreproducible bug; retain feature requests for manual decision. Preserve identity and source links; locally created issues stay local until explicitly published/linked.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Persist remote identity, observations, routed local work, import checkpoints and publication receipts. Deduplicate import/triage, coalesce updates and separate remote fields from local workflow, plan, pauses, budgets and private history. Use durable paced intake and outbox effects with echo suppression, bounded retries and observation-first recovery. Resolution publication binds verified completion/integration evidence; uncertain comment/close outcomes are reconciled before retry. Show queued/running/failed/conflicted state and authentication/rate-limit failures. Reopening a remote issue cannot clear a human pause or authorize resumed work.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Agents verify and incorporate GitHub clarification about the same bug. Genuinely new scope or feature requests are held for a user decision with an in-app notification. Agents reconcile other conflicting updates automatically, retaining both versions, provenance and rationale. If unresolved, preserve both versions and escalate through the approval queue with an in-app notification. Only conflicting changes and affected work wait; unrelated work continues. Reconciliation cannot override user directions, permissions or pauses, or publish intermediate local execution details.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Locally created issues stay local until explicitly published to GitHub or linked to an existing GitHub issue. Creation/editing never implicitly publishes or links them. After explicit linking/publication, apply inbound updates and verified-resolution publication under GH-05; retain local identity/history and configured permissions. Do not mirror every local edit or workflow status to GitHub.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Automatically import existing open GitHub issues when connecting a repository and every newly reported issue thereafter. Queue automatic agent triage app-wide, admitting at most one issue every 30 minutes by default, with the interval configurable in Settings. Keep waiting issues visible without starting agents or catch-up bursts. Triage bug reports versus feature requests, verify reported bugs and immediately start verifiable bugs under existing execution controls. Notify in-app for feature requests or unverifiable bugs. Shared repositories have no single issue-owning project: triage routes incoming reports to relevant project context. Projects retain their own issues/features; feature coordinators and the message board coordinate overlapping work.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use direct GitHub API polling from the Rust application to discover relevant repository, push, PR/merge, issue, review and check/workflow changes. Use authenticated conditional requests where supported, respecting GitHub rate limits, retry guidance and endpoint poll-interval headers. No webhook receiver, public endpoint, tunnel or relay is required. Poll while the app is open and reconcile remote state after reopening, sleep/wake or connectivity recovery. Remote-state reconciliation must not replay missed scheduled inference runs or implicitly resume paused work.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Changes discovered by GitHub polling must produce application events used both to notify relevant agents/coordinators and to trigger appropriate repository indexing updates. Events must retain their source repository and relevant work/PR context so notifications and index changes can be inspected alongside the affected work. Code-affecting changes such as pushes and merges must cause the affected indexed code to be refreshed; issue/review-only changes must not require a code reindex. Preserve source revision and visible index freshness.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Persist observed GitHub state and deduplicated application events in the existing SQLite runtime, with separate delivery/progress state for agent notification and indexing consumers. Repeated polls/restarts must not duplicate agent notices or indexing side effects. Deliver events to the responsible agent sessions as inspectable external updates without replacing user directions or clearing pauses; show undelivered updates. For code events, reconcile the affected configured ref/revision with remote content before incremental indexing, coalesce redundant pending refreshes and expose queued/running/failed/stale state and logs. An index failure must not suppress the corresponding agent event. Define initial baselines, event ordering, polling cadence, indexed-ref scope and replay/recovery mechanics before implementation.
requirements.validationFamily: Conditional polling, sync conflict and event-consumer tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Settings must provide an explicit Auto-Merge on/off control, enabled by default with project and repository overrides. The target autonomous workflow supports committing, pushing, responding to reviews, fixing findings, and merging without routine human intervention. With Auto-Merge off, the workflow must stop before merge while other authorized work may continue.
requirements.validationFamily: Head-bound review/fix/barrier/release-policy tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Mandatory independent code review before merge defaults to on, with project/repository overrides and a separate-agent fix/review cycle. Configured GitHub automated reviews normally satisfy it. Use an independent in-app reviewer when automation is absent, fails or never completes. Automation failure must not indefinitely prevent delivery; fallback still requires complete review and resolution of every actionable finding.
requirements.validationFamily: Head-bound review/fix/barrier/release-policy tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Use configured GitHub review automation normally; automatically fall back to an independent in-app reviewer if it fails or never completes. Avoid duplicate fallback launches. Bind review evidence and findings to the exact current head and source identity, including explicit completion with zero findings. Keep actionable external findings in the fix cycle even if fallback is used. Fallback satisfies the DevWorks review requirement without bypassing required checks, permissions or branch protection. Changed heads need current review evidence; all actionable findings must be resolved before merge.
requirements.validationFamily: Head-bound review/fix/barrier/release-policy tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Auto-Merge and mandatory-review policy must be configurable per repository with inherited defaults from project and workspace settings. Auto-Merge and mandatory independent review both default to on; project settings may override each inherited value, and repository settings may override each project value. The effective value and source of each value, including local overrides, must be visible. One repository’s review setup must not be assumed to apply to every repository in its project.
requirements.validationFamily: Head-bound review/fix/barrier/release-policy tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Every actionable review finding must be resolved before an automatic merge, including minor findings. A severity threshold alone must not permit unresolved actionable findings. The feature coordinator adjudicates disputed or non-actionable findings, recording its rationale in the linked review history. Findings it judges actionable must still be fixed.
requirements.validationFamily: Head-bound review/fix/barrier/release-policy tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Merge readiness must reconcile the current code revision, required checks, the review source selected under DELIVERY-02–03, all actionable findings, effective policy, and cross-repository dependencies. Apply the effective repository review and Auto-Merge policy to both task/group PRs into the feature branch and the final feature PR into main. Review findings, fixes, re-reviews, dismissals and reasons must remain linked to the feature, PR, revision, and participating agents.
requirements.validationFamily: Head-bound review/fix/barrier/release-policy tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The maximum number of fix/review cycles must be configurable in Settings, with a default of 3. Execution must honor the configured limit rather than continue an unbounded fix loop. Reaching the limit does not waive the requirement to resolve every actionable finding before merge.
requirements.validationFamily: Head-bound review/fix/barrier/release-policy tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: If the feature coordinator cannot reach a decision, it must raise the issue to the user and publish an in-app notification. This applies to unresolved review disputes or fix-cycle outcomes it cannot resolve. The escalation must retain the relevant findings, attempts, evidence, and coordinator rationale; unresolved actionable findings continue to block that merge. Escalation must not pause independent feature work: only the affected task and its dependent work wait.
requirements.validationFamily: Head-bound review/fix/barrier/release-policy tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide separate settings for agent-initiated deployments and release publishing. Each has Automatic, Ask me and Disabled values and defaults to Ask me. Inherit workspace defaults through project settings, with independent per-repository overrides; show effective values and their sources. These controls are independent of each other and of Auto-Merge. Ask me requires explicit user approval before the action; Disabled prevents it; Automatic permits it subject to existing tool permissions and applicable execution rules. A merge is not deployment or release approval. Harness self-improvement installation/restart still requires explicit approval under SELF-03.
requirements.validationFamily: Head-bound review/fix/barrier/release-policy tests
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Users must be able to manage which tools agents can access, primarily through Settings. Management must cover built-in application tools, tools supplied by MCP servers and package-provided tools.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared selection, role and nested-operation enforcement
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The effective tool set must be inspectable for an agent/session, derived from the shared selection under TOOL-04 and the mandatory reviewer restriction under TOOL-05. MCP defaults follow MCP-06. Shell/process and web defaults follow TOOL-06 and TOOL-08. Define remaining built-in defaults, denial precedence, and effects on queued and active runs. Disabled tools must be enforced at invocation time rather than merely omitted from prompts.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared selection, role and nested-operation enforcement
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Record tool policy revisions and changes with actor attribution. Tool descriptions and schemas are not authority to exceed user policy. Preserve explicit user selections during tool discovery. Define how read-only classification is established, how missing or conflicting metadata is handled, and how later tool additions or capability changes affect saved selections. Initial MCP defaults and selection controls follow MCP-06.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared selection, role and nested-operation enforcement
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The configured tool selection applies to every agent, rather than requiring separate selections for coordinators, coding agents, and reviewers. Code-review agents must have access to the same selected read tools as the other agents.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared selection, role and nested-operation enforcement
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Code-review agents must always be read-only. The harness must deny write/edit and other mutating operations, including indirect writes through shell/process tools, while preserving the shared selected read tools. Enforce this for built-in, MCP and package-provided invocations, not only in reviewer instructions; Settings and Select all must not override it. The harness retains review findings and history without granting the reviewer general write access. Fixes belong to separately authorized implementation agents.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared selection, role and nested-operation enforcement
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Enable built-in shell/process tools by default for implementation agents, subject to configured tool permissions and project scope. Users may disable them in Settings. Default enablement must not grant review agents write access or bypass TOOL-05.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared selection, role and nested-operation enforcement
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Implementation agents may install project dependencies automatically within authorized project/worktree scope. System-wide tool or package installations require user approval before execution. Configured permissions and read-only reviewer restrictions still apply. Record installation actions and approval outcomes in the associated work history.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared selection, role and nested-operation enforcement
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide built-in web search and page-fetching tools, including documentation retrieval, enabled by default. Apply shared tool selection and invocation permissions, including access for read-only review agents. Retain tool activity, source URLs and results in the responsible agent/work history.
requirements.validationFamily: Shared selection, role and nested-operation enforcement
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Provide a general harness package system using managed executables and a Rust SDK, sharing versioned installation and lifecycle infrastructure with language packs. Packages may contribute agent tools, commands, workflow steps and verification gates, event handlers, context retrieval and compaction extensions, skills, prompts and role instructions, and native UI contributions. Provider extensions must register through the router rather than create a separate inference path. Support local package development and independently installable prebuilt packages without recompiling the main app. Building Rust packages locally requires the appropriate development toolchain; installing compatible prebuilt packages does not. Core use must not require a TypeScript/Bun/Node runtime.
requirements.validationFamily: Every contribution kind, approval and guarded version transition
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Agents must be able to create and test a package project, explain its capabilities and changes, and propose it for activation. Agent-authored new or changed executable packages require explicit user approval before activation, including updates to active packages. Bind approval to the reviewed package version and contents; record rationale, requested capabilities, dependencies, verification evidence and originating agent/work. Pending or rejected proposals leave the active version unchanged. Package development and tests use authorized worktrees and tool permissions; packaged skills and role-instruction changes retain SKILL-07–09 and SET-05–06 approval rules. Approval to activate a package does not grant approval for every action it later requests.
requirements.validationFamily: Every contribution kind, approval and guarded version transition
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Package UI contributions must use host-defined descriptions of settings pages, forms, tables, reports, panels, actions and status indicators rendered natively by egui. Packages may request host dialogs and notifications through the same application interfaces. Do not require a WebView or exchange egui objects across the executable boundary. Packages can extend the UI within supported contribution points without rebuilding the host; completely new widget types or host extension points may require a host update. Exact schemas and supported component coverage remain to be specified.
requirements.validationFamily: Every contribution kind, approval and guarded version transition
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Package actions must use the shared application command/query and tool interfaces and retain project scope, tool selection, read-only reviewer restrictions, work ownership, concurrency/resource limits, plan approval and review/delivery gates. All package-requested inference must pass through the internal router. Context and compaction contributions must preserve original transcripts, user directions, required context and the configured compaction threshold; avoid unnecessary cache changes and record context provenance. Extensions may add checks but must not silently remove required gates. Managed executable separation is not an OS security sandbox: host checks govern brokered operations, and restricting arbitrary native file or network access would require OS isolation. Document the executable trust model honestly.
requirements.validationFamily: Every contribution kind, approval and guarded version transition
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Broaden Settings Add-ons into one management screen for language packs and general harness packages. Show package type, source, version, contributions, scope, requested/effective access, prerequisites, compatibility, health and logs. Provide install, update, configure, enable, disable and uninstall controls and access to approval proposals. Approved new versions reload at the next safe boundary, retaining the prior version for rollback and recording which package version each agent used. Preserve package state and linked activity through restart; visible failures must not stall unrelated authorized work. Exact state migration, rollback compatibility and active-run transition mechanics remain proposed implementation details.
requirements.validationFamily: Every contribution kind, approval and guarded version transition
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Extend the common manifest and local process protocol with declared contributions, configuration schemas, scoped host calls, event subscriptions and package state access. The host owns registration, validates messages and results, and attributes tools, commands, hooks, state and UI actions to package/version, agent/session and applicable work. Separate notifications from bounded decision or transformation hooks; define ordering, timeouts, errors and recovery so a failed extension cannot leave a required decision looking successful. Persist subscription progress and action identities where replay is supported to prevent duplicate external effects. Apply package-version changes at explicit safe boundaries and reconcile state before rollback. Protocol details, distribution/trust, dependency resolution, SDK APIs and native UI schemas remain open.
requirements.validationFamily: Every contribution kind, approval and guarded version transition
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Independent tool calls must keep running when another call fails or requires approval, unless that failure makes their execution unsafe or invalid. Hold or cancel only affected calls and their actual dependents. Preserve completed results and reconcile uncertain effects before retry. Existing parent pauses and tool permissions remain effective.
requirements.validationFamily: Independent-call completion, scoped failures/waits, ordered wire results and crash recovery
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: After the user explicitly trusts a publisher for package updates, allow compatible signed updates to activate automatically at a safe boundary provided access does not expand beyond the approved scope. Expanded access requires fresh approval. New or changed agent-authored executable contents still require explicit approval of the exact version and contents under EXT-02, even if signed by a trusted publisher. Preserve active work, prior outcomes and rollback/state compatibility; publisher trust does not authorize future actions outside normal tool, role, work and permission controls.
requirements.validationFamily: Signed update authority, exact agent approval and guarded activation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: The app must provide a way to navigate code graphs and their relationships, move between entities and their source context, and inspect graph information within repository and project scope.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Scoped node/source/relationship navigation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Follow the existing CodeGraph repository home and navigation as the baseline for repository exploration. Opening a repository leads to its Overview, with Nodes, Health, and Reviews available directly. Preserve repository identity and indexed revision/freshness, summary and confidence, health and activity indicators, internal code-project analysis, inbound/outbound dependencies, node-type counts and drill-down, and README where available. The workspace coordinator chat remains the application opening screen.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Scoped node/source/relationship navigation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Preserve the CodeGraph drill-down from a repository or internal code project into a node list, optionally filtered by node type, with grouped node kinds, expandable containers and members, and links to node details. Node details retain qualified name, properties, trust/confidence, source location and line-numbered source, and incoming/outgoing relationships grouped by type. Related nodes and cross-repository relationships must be navigable, with breadcrumbs back to repository and node-type context.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Scoped node/source/relationship navigation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Adapt the accepted navigation flow to egui and the multi-repository project model without copying Angular routing or web hosting. Internal code projects/modules must be distinguished from top-level work projects that group repositories. Preserve repository context across home, list and detail views; provide return navigation to the originating workspace. Extra graph visualization controls and saved views remain open rather than replacing the accepted repository home.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Scoped node/source/relationship navigation
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Database indexing must be supported alongside repository indexing. The app must manage database indexing sources and connections, including a file path for SQLite or another supported file-backed database.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Metadata-only, project/connection policy and actual read-only boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: A database source must declare engine/adapter, display identity, project associations and effective access, file path or connection endpoint, credential references where needed, enabled state, schema selection, and indexing status. Reuse one connection definition across project associations under DB-09. Creating, editing, testing, disabling, reindexing, and removing indexed metadata must be available without deleting or modifying the source database.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Metadata-only, project/connection policy and actual read-only boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Schema indexing must use read-only source access and extract supported tables, columns, types, keys, indexes, views, procedures and relationships. Report coverage per adapter. Indexing does not read row contents into a searchable data index. Agent queries and data mutations are separate operations under DB-04–05.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Metadata-only, project/connection policy and actual read-only boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Database indexing covers schemas only and remains read-only. Separately provide agent tools to read and manipulate data. Each database connection defaults to read-only; data writes require explicit user enablement for that connection. Enforce connection policy together with configured tool permissions and project scope. Enabling writes on one connection must not enable them on others. Code-review agents remain read-only even when connection writes are enabled.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Metadata-only, project/connection policy and actual read-only boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Expose database data tools against configured target connections, with visible effective read/write permissions and project scope. Support queries and permitted data inserts, updates and deletes, with adapter-specific capability reporting, execution/result limits, cancellation and attributed history. Enforce read-only access at the execution/connection boundary where supported, including indirect mutations; SQL keyword checks alone are insufficient. Under DB-08, link schema changes to their migration commit or direct operation, recording the fallback reason and outcome. Define transaction, failure/retry and sensitive-result handling without importing row data into the schema index.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Metadata-only, project/connection policy and actual read-only boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Support SQLite, MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server as target database families for schema indexing and separately permissioned data tools. MariaDB and MySQL must both be covered and verified, with differences reported. These are target connections, independent of the selected SQLite and sqlite-vec internal app storage. Supported engine versions, authentication modes and metadata coverage remain to be qualified. HelixDB and HydraDB are excluded from target readers.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Metadata-only, project/connection policy and actual read-only boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Do not implement a HelixDB schema reader or structural-inference adapter. The user removed this conditional capability on 2 November 2026. Retain historical storage evaluations only as evidence; they neither enable HelixDB connections nor add an internal storage dependency. Schema indexing for the selected relational targets remains metadata-only, with separately permissioned data tools governed by DB-04–06.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Metadata-only, project/connection policy and actual read-only boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Agents may change database schemas, including supported CREATE, ALTER and DROP operations. Prefer migration files committed to the appropriate project repository through its normal worktree, review and delivery workflow. If committed migrations are not possible, direct schema changes are allowed. Applying either route requires writes to be explicitly enabled for the target connection and the agent to have the necessary tool permissions and project scope. A migration commit alone does not authorize application to a database. Indexing and code-review agents remain read-only. Preserve the associated task, agent and action history.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Metadata-only, project/connection policy and actual read-only boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Database connections may be shared across multiple projects, with access controlled per project. Sharing a connection must not automatically grant access to other projects or their agents. Resolve the requesting project and enforce its access together with the connection settings and agent tool permissions on every operation. Project access cannot enable writes while the connection remains read-only. Indexing and code-review agents remain read-only even where project and connection settings permit writes. Retain project and responsible-agent attribution for operations against shared connections.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Metadata-only, project/connection policy and actual read-only boundary
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Users must be able to navigate indexed schemas, inspect their objects and relationships, and understand their connection to code or project work. File-backed database sources must not require an application storage server.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Objects/relationships/freshness/capability display
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Schema exploration should support object search, table/column details, keys and constraints, relationship traversal, source identity, sync freshness and failures, and code-to-schema references where evidence supports them. Unsupported metadata must not appear as confirmed absent.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Objects/relationships/freshness/capability display
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Repository health analysis must be visible in the UI, with access to analysis results and the findings that need attention. This is distinct from the health of the app, its stores, or its background workers.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Revision-bound evidence, partial/failure and coverage behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Health results must identify repository/revision, analysis time, coverage, categories and severity where supported, evidence, trends where available, and linked corrective work. Missing, stale, partial, or failed analysis must be distinguished from a healthy result. Scoring and remediation automation remain open.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces
requirements.validationFamily: Revision-bound evidence, partial/failure and coverage behavior
requirements.designStatus: Proposed architecture mapping; not an implementation/test result

requirements.statement: Code reviews must have a visible management and inspection surface, linked to repositories, features, source changes, PRs, and the agents or users who produced and addressed the findings.
requirements.sourceSection: 19 Graph schema health and review workspaces

requirements.statement: Completed and stopped work must be graded automatically from durable history without re-running it: coordinator and worker transcripts and tool calls, Git, PR and review records, and the resulting work state. This covers DevWorks’s own coordinator and worker sessions and the attributed command records of external harnesses connected as MCP clients under MCP-10; DevWorks holds no external harness transcripts and does not import them. Attribute graded behavior at the step level to the revisions in effect when it happened (skills, roles, overrides, conventions, rules, routing and running app version). A session can span several revisions under SKILL-05; a result that cannot be attributed to one revision belongs to an explicit mixed-revision group, never silently to one side. Grading reads only and never changes work, repositories, remotes or Knowledge.

requirements.statement: Support deterministic checks over the event record, outcome checks over work state, model-graded rubrics through the internal router, and human verdicts. Every grader names the requirement, skill section or rule it enforces, and a check that measures only a proxy, such as a command pattern rather than intent, says so. A model-graded result records the judge model and settings, rubric revision, sampled instances and their population, and each verdict with its reason; each instance receives several independent votes and split votes are reported. A judge verdict is never presented as a deterministic result. A judge configuration is calibrated against human verdicts on a sample before its results can gate approval under EVAL-05, and its agreement rate is shown with its results; changing the judge model, settings or rubric is a measurement change under EVAL-06. All model-based judging, including production grading, is live inference under TEST-03; tests of the eval machinery use scripted judges and fixtures under TEST-02.

requirements.statement: Support repeatable trials that run agent work against frozen inputs, such as snapshots of work records and repository revisions, in an isolated workspace. Trials may write only to disposable copies: throwaway repositories and remotes and stateful substitutes for the tracker, GitHub and other external services, so claiming, implementation, review and delivery can be evaluated end to end. Production destinations, real accounts and real credentials are unreachable from a trial; a case may also refuse all writes. Substitute services expose the real services’ tool schemas. Each case runs a configured number of times, and results report each run’s score, the share of runs that passed and whether every run passed. Trials are live inference under TEST-03 and never run within unit or integration tests. Each snapshot records its source, time, content identity and expected answer.

requirements.statement: Every change to an evaluable subject under EVAL-01 must carry eval evidence. For changes that need approval, run the applicable trials against the baseline and the candidate before the proposal is presented. For changes that take effect without approval, including user-saved edits, dreaming consolidations under DREAM-05 and user routing changes, record the comparison when it can run and always monitor after adoption under EVAL-07; evaluation adds no approval step where none exists. The comparison shows the target metric’s change and every other metric’s change with its method and uncertainty under EVAL-09, the run count and coverage under EVAL-14. Evidence is labeled improved, regressed, inconclusive or unvalidated. It is unvalidated when no applicable suite exists, the suite could not run or either arm falls below the suite’s minimum sample or coverage; inconclusive is reserved for an adequately measured comparison without a meaningful difference. For an agent-authored change, regressed or unvalidated evidence blocks approval unless the user overrides it with a recorded reason; inconclusive evidence is shown without blocking. The user’s own edits carry evidence without a gate. Eval evidence never replaces approval. Evidence is bound to immutable identities of the candidate and baseline, suite and case revisions, fixtures, grader and judge configurations, accepted exceptions and trial settings. Both arms use the same measurement revisions and settings except the declared subject under test; when that subject is a routing or model assignment, all other settings including the judge stay the same. Approval binds to the evaluated candidate; a later change to the candidate or to a measurement input it depends on returns the proposal to unvalidated until re-evaluated.

requirements.validationFamily: Revision-attributed grading, isolated trials, evidence coverage and approval controls

requirements.statement: A subject under evaluation must not be able to change its own measurement. Agents may draft suites, cases, graders, rubrics and fixtures; activating them requires user approval as a separate proposal with its own history. One proposal must not change both a subject and a suite that measures it. Accepted exceptions are authored by a person and record the check, matched instance, reason and approver.

requirements.statement: After a change is adopted, production grading continues and compares the new revision with the previous one under EVAL-09. When a monitored metric regresses past its declared criterion, notify the user with the evidence and propose a rollback; a rollback never happens without user approval. Use the subject’s own activation mechanism: SKILL-08 revision-aware rollback for skills, roles and overrides; the revision and lifecycle mechanisms of CONV-02, KNOW-03 and DREAM-04 for conventions and lesson rules; the settings revision for role routing; and reinstallation of a prior build for app builds, which also requires SELF-03 approval, a compatibility check of stored data and migrations made since that build, and the SELF-02 restart and rollback mechanics. A build whose data changes cannot be safely reversed is reported as not rollback-capable, with the reason. A rollback preserves later unrelated edits or reports the conflict without overwriting them, and is monitored like any other change.

requirements.statement: Failing checks must trace to the rule, skill section or lesson they enforce, with links to the exact transcript, tool call or record under HISTORY-01. Recurring failures should become candidate improvements in the Knowledge and dreaming flow with their eval evidence attached, such as a skill or role edit, hook, test or harness-code task, and feed the lesson recurrence views of KNOW-04 and KNOW-05. Before a failure becomes a proposal, sampled failing instances are checked so a grader defect is not reported as agent behavior, and that check and its outcome are recorded.

requirements.statement: Results show counts with denominators, runs, coverage and revision groups, never a bare percentage. Each metric declares its comparison method, uncertainty measure and minimum effect; for example, a binary outcome reports the difference in proportions with a confidence interval, and a judged rubric includes the judge calibration. A difference whose uncertainty includes no change, or that falls short of the declared minimum effect, is inconclusive, and improvement is never claimed from a single run or case. Requirements fix no numeric thresholds; suites start with values labeled provisional, which are replaced by measured values and are never acceptance thresholds. Trial comparisons match cases, fixtures, models, tools, budgets and measurement revisions in both arms except the declared subject under test. Production comparisons use common measurement revisions for both cohorts, regrading retained evidence under one revision where available; otherwise the comparison is non-comparable and never triggers a regression notice or rollback proposal. Production comparisons disclose cohort differences in task mix and size, projects, models, routing and other revisions changed in the same period; a change coinciding with another change to the same behavior is reported as confounded. Where possible, validation uses cases other than those that motivated a proposal, and results say which were which.

requirements.statement: Expose a Documents area within the Knowledge workspace, backed by the same document ingestion and retrieval operations available through configured agent tools. Support adding local files using a selection dialog or drag and drop, inspecting source text and indexing status, searching the corpus, opening a result at its source passage, reindexing, disabling and removing a document from active retrieval. Include explicit sharing and Move to project controls under RAG-11. Show title, source, tags, project/shared scope, version, indexed time, chunk counts and errors. Imported documents are managed project artifacts under RAG-12. Removing an index must not silently delete an external original or the retained managed artifact; artifact deletion follows the existing explicit deletion and shared-reference rules. A chat attachment is not automatically a durable corpus document unless explicitly added or covered by a configured ingestion rule.

requirements.statement: Use a staged pipeline for supported document formats: extract text and structural locators, normalize it, split it into meaningful bounded chunks, generate embeddings through the internal router, and publish searchable chunks with source provenance. Markdown, plain text, PDF and Word documents are required under RAG-09. Initial Word ingestion supports modern .docx only under RAG-09; native extraction adapters remain to qualify. Routed vision fallback for scanned pages is confirmed under RAG-10. Report unsupported or encrypted sources and failed extraction honestly rather than marking empty content successfully indexed. Folder watching, remote URL ingestion and additional formats remain open choices; no mandatory preinstalled Node, Python or office runtime may be introduced into core use.

requirements.statement: Support user-added Markdown, plain text, PDF and Word documents for knowledge ingestion, indexing and retrieval. These four document formats are required initial capabilities, not optional future formats. Apply the same indexing visibility, source provenance, project scope and agent retrieval requirements to each. Initial Word support is modern .docx only; legacy binary .doc is excluded from initial support. Scanned or image-only pages use the configurable routed vision fallback under RAG-10. Do not silently report failed or empty extraction as successful indexing.

requirements.statement: Extract existing document text directly where available, and use a configured vision-capable model through the internal router as the fallback for scanned or image-only pages. Enable this vision extraction fallback by default. Expose the fallback and its model/route configuration in Settings, with enable/disable control. This pathway must not require a separate bundled OCR model or local inference runtime; a user-selected local vision endpoint may have its own optional runtime. Save the extracted text with the source document revision/content hash, page identity and extraction model provenance, preserving access to the original page. Reuse that extraction for indexing and retrieval until the source changes or re-extraction is explicitly requested, rather than repeating vision inference on each search. Chunking and embedding remain separate subsequent steps, and their inference also goes through the router. Show extraction progress, usage/costs and failures; if fallback is disabled or no capable route is available, mark affected pages as requiring extraction or partially indexed rather than silently claiming completion. Page rendering/batching, language coverage and quality acceptance remain to confirm.

requirements.statement: Offer hybrid lexical and vector retrieval so exact names, identifiers and terms remain searchable alongside semantic matches. Return bounded passages with source identity, revision/content hash, chunk identity and heading, page or other supported locator. Rank and deduplicate results, expose the retrieval mode and useful score information without presenting a similarity score as factual confidence. Where evidence supports a generated answer, provide navigable source citations; preserve retrieved source revisions and citations in the session/work history. Do not invent evidence when the corpus has no suitable result. Graph expansion linking documents to code, entities, features or tasks is a candidate enhancement; the precise ranking, fusion, reranking and graph traversal policy remains open.

requirements.statement: Enforce existing project/shared Knowledge scope and tool permissions before materializing retrieved content, including vector candidates, snippets, graph expansion and caches. Adding a document must not make it available across every project merely because it is indexed or tagged as a lesson. Show its effective scope; default project association, explicit sharing and moving are confirmed under RAG-11. Scope changes must reconcile retrieval filters and caches so former project associations do not continue granting future access. Exact sharing representation and update consistency mechanics remain to specify. Preserve the distinction between source text, derived claims and verified knowledge. Retrieved text is evidence and cannot override user directions, role authority or configured tool permissions. Database schema indexing remains metadata-only; this document requirement does not authorize importing database row values.

requirements.statement: Track source identity/content hash, extraction/chunking version, embedding model identity/revision and vector dimensions. Reuse unchanged valid chunks, reconcile edited and removed sources, and avoid mixing incompatible embedding spaces after a model change. Keep failed, partial, stale and completed indexing distinguishable with per-document and per-run logs, progress, cancellation and retry. Publish complete replacements without silently serving mixed source revisions; define retention of prior versions under existing artifact/history rules. Reopening the app must preserve the corpus, completed indexes and attributable interrupted operations; exact checkpoint and rebuild mechanics remain to specify.

requirements.statement: All embedding, query embedding, model-based extraction, reranking, summarization and answer generation must follow the internal router whenever they perform inference, including any reused library or package. Show effective models, provider availability, attributable usage/costs and failures. Precomputed local vector and lexical search must not require a separate database server. If an embedding provider is unavailable, expose reduced lexical-only retrieval where supported rather than claiming vector search succeeded. Help must still satisfy its entirely local offline search requirement under HELP-05; using shared retrieval primitives must not make Help depend on a network embedding request. Route selection and availability of an optional local embedding model remain implementation decisions.

requirements.statement: Keep managed document contents and extracted text in local file storage, durable corpus/indexing metadata and jobs in SQLite, and document vectors in sqlite-vec with evidence/graph relationships in application-owned SQLite tables. Exact ownership, lexical indexing and consistency mechanics remain subject to STORE-03 and OPEN 08. Reuse common retrieval capabilities for documents, conventions and unified Knowledge without duplicating authoritative records. OxiRS is an evaluated candidate for selected reusable Rust components, not an approved additional store or replacement for SQLite, sqlite-vec, the router or the harness. Before selection, validate actual behavior, dependency/footprint impact, supported platforms, adapters, persistence, scope enforcement and recovery with representative documents; add no RDF/SPARQL service or third persistent store without an explicit architecture decision.

requirements.statement: Newly added knowledge documents default to the current project. Users must be able to explicitly share a document across projects and move it to another project, including to correct adding it to the wrong project. Expose these controls in the document manager and through agent tools subject to configured permissions. Moving changes the current project association rather than requiring deletion and re-upload; preserve document identity, source provenance and attributed move history. The previous project must not retain future retrieval access solely because it was the original owner; any continued access must come from explicit sharing. Preserve existing historical evidence under its access rules rather than rewriting original provenance or claiming prior agent exposure can be undone. Adding documents without a current project and the precise sharing controls remain to specify.

requirements.statement: Keep a DevWorks-managed copy of every imported knowledge document and treat it as a project artifact. Index and retrieve from this managed copy so moving or deleting the external original does not break the knowledge library. Retain the original source location as provenance without making retrieval depend on that path continuing to exist. Apply artifact identity, project scope, sharing, retention until explicit deletion and shared-reference preservation rules; link the document to its originating feature/task when applicable rather than inventing a work association for a project-only import. Document scope/move operations under RAG-11 must operate on the same managed document/artifact identity. Removing or rebuilding a search index does not delete the underlying artifact. Updating from a changed external original and replacement mechanics remain to specify; retain all managed versions until explicitly deleted under RAG-13.

requirements.statement: Replacing an imported document must create a new managed version and retain every prior version until explicitly deleted. Bind historical citations to the exact version originally used; replacement must not silently redirect them to new content. Version deletion follows artifact permissions and shared-reference preservation rules, and retained citations must show unavailable/deleted content honestly rather than resolve to different bytes. Rebuilding indexes, feature completion and storage pressure must not expire retained document versions.

requirements.statement: Keep the architecture clean and purposeful: give each component a clear responsibility, make dependency directions and ownership explicit, avoid redundant code and duplicated authoritative state, and reuse common implementations wherever behavior is genuinely shared. UI actions and agent tools should reuse the same application capabilities. Prefer the minimum abstraction that solves an established need; reuse must not become speculative frameworks, unnecessary layers or forced inheritance. Record the rationale for important boundaries and tradeoffs.

requirements.statement: Design every important part of the code to be testable. Separate core decisions and state transitions from side effects through explicit, replaceable boundaries for storage, provider transport, processes, files, clocks and other nondeterministic inputs where needed. Important logic must be exercisable without launching the desktop UI, connecting to a real provider or relying on global mutable state. The later suite is separate planned work; it is not required to be set up or run during requirements capture.
